review: code view, checklist code-change C1-C16 and C25

findings.path: Document C declares parent P. Its object C-2 has links/C-2.xml with a link to X/X-9; X is not a parent of C and X-9 doesn't exist. Validation reports LINK_NOT_ALLOWED for the link (validator._check_link_policy). The suspect scan classifies the same link BROKEN; _problems skips a BROKEN line only when link_target_missing() is true, which needs target_doc == doc.id, so it appends a second line 'C: BROKEN C-2 -> X/X-9 (target file missing)'.
findings.impact: One wrong link is printed and counted as two check problems. The trace comment above the code claims one line per check problem, and SRS-33's rationale says such a link gets LINK_NOT_ALLOWED alone.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p2_gate.py, section 3 (output in p2.out): mellon-check prints 'C: LINK_NOT_ALLOWED links/C-2.xml: link to X/X-9 is not allowed ...' and 'C: BROKEN C-2 -> X/X-9 (target file missing)' for the one link, and its summary counts 5 problems for 4.
findings.fix: In _problems, also skip the BROKEN line when the link's target_doc isn't the document or one of its declared parents, since LINK_NOT_ALLOWED already reports it. Better: build SRS-35 and SRS-140 together, so a broken link is only ever reported once, as a validation error. Test: one link to a missing object in a document that isn't a parent; expect exactly one line.

findings.path: (a) A load error that isn't an XML syntax error, such as an object file whose stem doesn't match its id: _doc_load_error takes the line only from an lxml XMLSyntaxError cause ('line = getattr(err.__cause__, "lineno", None)'), so line is None. (b) A manifest error raised without a path prefix ('<parent> missing required @doc', '<attribute> requires @name and @kind', 'kind=enum has no <option>s', '<ref> missing required @id'): _error_file finds no path, so file is None too. (c) mellon-check prints only '{doc_id}: LOAD_ERROR {message}' and never prints DocLoadError.file or .line, so file and line appear only when the loader's message happens to hold them.
findings.impact: The person fixing a broken file after a merge isn't told which line, and for some manifest errors not even which file. validate_repo and repo_health return file null and line null for these; mellon-check's line holds neither. SRS-137 (Accepted) and SRS-90/-102 (Implemented) require file and line for each load error, and the definitions say a load error has the file, line and reason.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p2_gate.py, section 3: mellon-check prints 'M: LOAD_ERROR <parent> missing required @doc' (no file, no line) and 'B: LOAD_ERROR ...B-1.xml: filename stem 'B-1' does not match @id='B-2'' (no line). MCP validate_repo/repo_health return {'doc_id': 'M', 'file': None, 'line': None} and {'doc_id': 'B', 'file': 'B/objects/B-1.xml', 'line': None}. Only the XML syntax error (doc S) has line 3.
findings.fix: Give LoaderError explicit file and line fields: the file the loader was parsing (pass the manifest path into _parse_parents/_parse_attributes/_parse_refs) and the offending element's sourceline (lxml keeps it); line 1 or the root element's line when nothing narrower applies. Have _doc_load_error copy them instead of parsing the message, and print them in mellon-check: 'LOAD_ERROR <doc> <file>:<line> <reason>'. Test: one load error of each kind the loader raises; expect a file and a line for each on all three surfaces.

findings.path: Rules file forbids Rationale on headings. Object D-1 has type Heading and '<attr name="Rationale"></attr>', so Rationale is set (definitions: set even when the file gives an empty value). _check_rules reads 'value = obj.attrs.get(attr_name, "").strip()' and reports only 'elif status == "forbidden" and value:', so the empty value passes.
findings.impact: SRS-61 (Implemented) as written, with the definition of set, requires RULE_FORBIDDEN_PRESENT here; the code reports nothing. The code instead does what SRS-60 (Proposed) asks: a blank value counts as not set. The requirement and the build state disagree, so a test case written from SRS-61 would fail.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p1_rules.py, case A (p1.out): codes [] for the empty value; control with Rationale='why' gives RULE_FORBIDDEN_PRESENT. p7_buildstate.py: a value of three spaces is also not reported (the loader strips it), but a value of U+200B is, so SRS-60 is only partly built.
findings.fix: Question for the person (agent rule 3): if blank should count as not set, accept SRS-60, finish it (treat the zero-width characters the definition of blank lists as blank), and reword SRS-61 to a value that isn't blank. Otherwise report RULE_FORBIDDEN_PRESENT when attr_name is in obj.attrs, whatever its value.

findings.path: A Document Editor is open on D (the GUI's service has the cache on). A pull, a merge or an agent leaves conflict markers in D/objects/D-1.xml. The user chooses Validate. _validate_current_doc calls validate_document, whose _load returns the cache hit without reading the disk, so the old copy is validated. The method doesn't check the stale flag either.
findings.impact: The status bar says 'D: validation passed.' for a document that now has a load error. SRS-2 says the load error is reported instead of a validation result. This is the case SRS-7 and SRS-80 (Proposed) describe, but SRS-2 is Implemented and unconditional.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p4_gui.py (offscreen, p4.out): after conflict markers are written into D-1.xml, _validate_current_doc leaves 'D: validation passed.' and shows no dialog. A fresh DocumentService(root).validate_document('D') on the same files raises the XML parse error.
findings.fix: Have the Validate action reload the document from the working copy (as F5 does) before it validates, and show the load error when the reload fails. That builds SRS-7 and SRS-80 too. Test: open the editor, corrupt a file, Validate; expect the load error and no 'passed'.

findings.path: A document with 12 validation errors. _validate_current_doc builds the dialog text from 'errors[:10]' and adds '... and 2 more'.
findings.impact: The Validate action doesn't show each validation error: from the 11th on, the user can't see which object is wrong or what the error is, only that more exist. SRS-79 requires each one.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p4_gui.py (offscreen, QMessageBox.warning captured): 'errors listed in the dialog: 10' for 12 errors; the last line reads '... and 2 more'.
findings.fix: Show every error, for example in a scrollable list or as the message box's detailed text, with code and message. Test: a document with more errors than fit on screen; expect each code and object in the dialog.

findings.path: Document C (parent P) holds objects C-1 and C-2. Its outline names C-1 twice and doesn't name C-2. C-2 links to P-1. coverage_report loops 'for obj_id in source.iter_outline_ids()', so it counts outline entries, not objects: C-1 twice, C-2 not at all.
findings.impact: repo_health reports that 0 of 2 of C's objects link to P; the true answer is 1 of 2. SRS-107 asks how many of the document's objects link to the parent, out of how many. The counts are wrong whenever the outline has a duplicate or misses an object; those documents do also get OUTLINE_DUP or OBJECT_NOT_IN_OUTLINE, but the coverage numbers give no hint. The same function serves TRACE's coverage_report tool and the PDF.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p3_health.py, section 1 (p3.out): outgoing row {'source_doc': 'C', 'target_doc': 'P', 'total': 2, 'covered': 0}.
findings.fix: Count each object of the document once: walk the outline, skip IDs already seen and IDs without an object, then add the objects the outline leaves out. Test: the probe's layout; expect 1 of 2.

findings.path: Document SRS has its rules in 'SRS/srs.rules.xml' (lower case). load_document looks for folder / f"{doc_id}.rules.xml" and _parse_rules_file tests path.is_file(). On Windows and macOS the file system ignores letter case, so the file is read as the rules file. On Linux (the Ubuntu CI job) is_file() is false and the document has no rules. The manifest lookup (has_manifest) checks the exact name for this reason; the rules file lookup doesn't.
findings.impact: The same commit validates differently on a Windows desktop and in Linux CI. An author who sees and fixes rule errors locally with a wrongly cased rules file gets a CI gate with every rule switched off, without a sign, so later rule breaches pass mellon-check.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p5_more.py, case A, run on win32: files ['SRS.xml', 'objects', 'srs.rules.xml'], 1 rule read, RULE_REQUIRED_MISSING reported. On Linux: analysis, since Path.is_file() on a case-sensitive file system finds no 'SRS.rules.xml'. Not run on Linux.
findings.fix: Find the rules file by its exact name in the folder listing, as has_manifest does, and report a load error for a file whose name matches <document ID>.rules.xml only when letter case is ignored. Test on both CI platforms.

findings.path: Document C declares parent P; C-1 links to P/P-9, which doesn't exist. Validation reports nothing, because LINK_TARGET_MISSING covers only the link's own document (SRS-35, the parent case, is Proposed). The suspect scan calls the link BROKEN, and mellon-check prints 'C: BROKEN C-1 -> P/P-9 (target file missing)' and exits 1.
findings.impact: The definitions name three check problems (load error, validation error, suspect link) and say a broken link is reported as a validation error. This link is reported under none of the three codes, validate_repo and the Validate action call the document clean, and the gate fails. Read literally, SRS-146 says exit 0 here. Read through the definition's last sentence, the link is a check problem but is reported without a validation error code. The code picks: fail, with a line of a fourth kind.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p5_more.py, case B (p5.out): validate(C) returns []; mellon-check exits 1 with 'C: BROKEN C-1 -> P/P-9 (target file missing)'.
findings.fix: Question for the person. Recommended: keep exit 1, and build SRS-35 with SRS-140, so this link becomes LINK_TARGET_MISSING on every surface and the BROKEN line goes away. Until then, say in the definition of check problem that a broken link into a parent document counts.

findings.path: repo_health calls scan_suspects(None) in 'try ... except ServiceError: suspect_scan = {}'. If the scan fails (the repository's .git moved or was replaced after the MCP server checked the root at start; a load error raised by scan_repo's own load), each document's suspect_count and total_suspect_count become 0, and the result carries no field that says the scan didn't run.
findings.impact: An agent's first look at the repository says 0 suspect links when Mellon couldn't work out a single link state. Per SRS-97 and SRS-101 these are counts of suspect links, and a failed scan reads as clean.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p3_health.py, section 4 (p3.out): with .git, C's suspect_count is 1 and total 1. After .git is renamed, it returns suspect_count 0 and total 0, with the same keys and no error.
findings.fix: Let the ServiceError through as a tool error, or return null counts with a scan_error field. Never return 0 for a scan that didn't run. Also drop the bare 'except Exception: pass' around the coverage rows, which would hide a coverage failure the same way.

findings.path: _problems reads the repository three times: validate_repo (load_all with load errors), get_all_documents (load_all again) and scan_suspects(None) -> scan_repo -> load_all(repo_root), which collects no load errors and skips a document that fails. If a file changes between the first and third read (mellon-check run locally while a git client pulls or checks out, or an agent writes), a document can validate clean in the first pass and then be dropped without a sign from the scan.
findings.impact: That document's suspect links aren't reported and its new load error isn't either, so mellon-check can exit 0 for a working copy that has a load error and suspect links. Unlikely in CI, possible on a desktop.
findings.proof: analysis: scan_repo calls load_all(repo_root) with load_errors=None (suspects.py:148), and load_all then skips a failing document ('continue', repo.py:181). Nothing compares the three loads. Unconfirmed: a race, not shown by a probe.
findings.fix: Load once: one load_all with load_errors, then validate each loaded document and scan it with scan_document on that same model. Then each document is either validated and scanned, or reported as a load error.

findings.path: Two rules both apply to D-1 and both require a link to document P (for example one for type Requirement and one for RequirementType Functional). D-1 has no link. _effective_link_directives extends the list with every matching rule's directives, so _check_rules appends RULE_LINK_REQUIRED_MISSING once per directive.
findings.impact: One missing link is reported twice with the same message: validate_repo's total_errors, repo_health's validation_error_count and mellon-check's problem count double. SRS-66 says a link is required to each document named, which suggests one error per document; the code gives one per directive.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p1_rules.py, case B (p1.out): [('RULE_LINK_REQUIRED_MISSING', 2)], two identical messages.
findings.fix: Report once per required target document: collect the target_doc values in a set before checking.

findings.path: repo_health loops 'for parent_id in doc.parents' and skips a parent that didn't load ('if parent_id not in docs: continue'). A parent declared twice gives both rows twice; a parent with a load error, or one the repository doesn't hold, gives no row.
findings.impact: SRS-107/-108 say 'for each pair of document and parent document' and don't say what a pair with a parent that doesn't load gets. The code drops it, so the coverage list shows no sign of the pair. load_errors names the parent when it fails to load, but a misspelt parent leaves no trace (SRS-38 is Proposed).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p3_health.py, section 2 (p3.out): parents ('P','P') gives 4 rows; P with conflict markers gives coverage [] and load_errors ['P'].
findings.fix: Decide with the person: return one row per distinct pair, and for a parent that doesn't load or doesn't exist a row with null counts and a reason.

findings.path: SRS-4 asks that each code keep the name the previous release used. The codes are string literals spread over eight functions, with no single list, and this review had no previous release to compare against (no history read, as instructed). Separately, the code already reports LINK_SOURCE_MISSING (SRS-37, Proposed) and treats whitespace-only values as not set in rule directives (part of SRS-60, Proposed). It still emits TABLE_BAD_ALIGN, TABLE_BAD_SPAN, TABLE_NO_COLUMNS and TABLE_GEOMETRY for documents built in memory, which SRS-4's rationale calls retired.
findings.impact: SRS-4 couldn't be checked, and a rename in one function would be easy to miss in review. The build states of SRS-37 and SRS-60 don't match the code.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/check/p7_buildstate.py (p7.out): '[LINK_SOURCE_MISSING] links/D-9.xml: source 'D-9' has no corresponding object'; a Rationale of three spaces isn't RULE_FORBIDDEN_PRESENT, one of U+200B is. SRS-4: not checked.
findings.fix: Keep the codes in one module-level table, and compare it with the previous release's table in a test. Ask the person to set SRS-37's status, with a test case, and to say whether the TABLE_ codes stay.

findings.path: A rules file holds a rule whose <then> has only a link directive (<link target-doc=...>), e.g. 'each Information object must link to SYS'. delete_attribute(any attribute) loops over every rule and removes each one where then_el.findall('attr') is empty, without looking at <link> directives or at whether this deletion removed anything.
findings.impact: Deleting any attribute, even one no rule names, silently deletes every link-only rule of the document. The CI gate stops checking required traceability and nothing says so; the Properties dialog's confirmation counts only attribute directives, so it doesn't warn either.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p1_delete_attr_drops_link_rules.py: rules before = [Heading/rationale forbidden, Information/link SYS required]; after delete_attribute('SW', 'priority') only the Heading rule is left in SW.rules.xml.
findings.fix: Remove a rule only when this deletion removed one of its <attr> directives and it then has neither <attr> nor <link> directives; test with a link-only rule and an attribute no rule names.

findings.path: New sibling calls svc.create_object(...) and then svc.move_object(new_id, after=sel): two @_recorded service calls, so _on_files_changed appends two undo steps for one action. The same holds for saving an edited filter under a new name (rename_filter, then set_filter_rules).
findings.impact: After New sibling the Undo action reads 'Undo move object'; one Undo moves the new object to the end of its parent instead of removing it, and a second Undo is needed. If the move fails, the object is left at the end and the action is half applied (MELLON-STORE-SRS-174 covers one operation).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p2_new_sibling_two_undo_steps.py: undo steps ['create object', 'move object']; Undo text '&Undo move object'; after one Undo the objects are D-0, D-1, D-2 with outline D-0, D-1, D-2 (D-2 still there).
findings.fix: Give create_object a position (after=) so New sibling is one service call, or wrap the action's calls in one journal and one undo step named for the action ('New sibling'); same for the filter rename-and-save.

findings.path: _populate_attrs iterates `attrs.items()`, the attributes set on the object, not doc.attributes. An attribute the object has no value for gets no field.
findings.impact: A new object shows no attribute fields at all in the Inspector, and an attribute that the active view hides and that the object has no value for can't be set anywhere in the Document Editor. The requirement's rationale ('an attribute that the active view hides can still be edited') fails exactly where it matters.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p4_inspector_unset_attrs.py: document attributes [type, rationale, priority], view 'no priority' active, object with type set: grid shows [type, rationale]; Inspector fields ['type'] only, so priority has no editor.
findings.fix: Build the Inspector form from doc.attributes (with the object's value or empty), keeping the rule-based hiding of forbidden empty attributes.

findings.path: Choosing a view stores the hidden column set per document in QSettings (grid/hidden_columns/<doc>). Every model reset re-applies that stored set, not the active view's list.
findings.impact: While a view is active, an attribute defined later shows although the view doesn't list it, and an attribute that an agent or another window adds to the view stays hidden after F5. A reviewer trusts a view that no longer shows what the view file says.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p5_view_columns_drift.py: view 'reviewer' lists ('rationale',); after defining 'priority' the shown columns are ['rationale', 'priority']; after the view file gains 'owner' and F5, shown = ['rationale', 'priority'] while the view lists ('rationale', 'owner').
findings.fix: While a view is active, derive the hidden set from the view's current list on every reset (and on views_changed); keep QSettings only for the no-view case.

findings.path: Dragging a column while a view is active calls set_view_visible(slug, _current_user_attr_order()). That helper returns every user attribute column in visual order, hidden ones included, although the comment says it passes 'exactly the currently-visible attrs'.
findings.impact: One column drag rewrites the shared view file to list every attribute of the document, so the next time anyone chooses the view all hidden columns show; the change is committed with the document.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p9_column_drag_view.py: view lists ('rationale', 'owner'); after one drag of 'owner' before 'rationale' the view lists ('owner', 'rationale', 'priority', 'phase').
findings.fix: Pass only the columns that aren't hidden (or the view's own names, reordered); add a test with a hidden attribute.

findings.path: Opening the Advanced filter dialog on a saved filter: a condition on an attribute the document no longer defines gets attr_combo index -1, so the row stays on entry 0 '(has outgoing link)' with op 'present'; an enumeration condition whose value is no longer an option gets _enum_combo index -1, so the row keeps the first option.
findings.impact: The dialog shows conditions the user never wrote, and OK saves them over the filter file: 'status ne Withdrawn' becomes 'status ne Draft' and 'owner is-empty' becomes 'has outgoing link present'. A review filter silently changes meaning (the case MELLON-EDIT-SRS-297's rationale keeps the filter loadable for).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p6_filter_dialog_rewrites.py: saved [('attr','status','ne','Withdrawn'), ('attr','owner','is-empty','')]; dialog would save [('attr','status','ne','Draft'), ('has-outgoing','','present','')].
findings.fix: When an attribute or option isn't found, add it to the combo as an 'unknown' entry (as AttrDelegate does for values) and keep the stored text, or refuse to open the row for editing and say why.

findings.where: MELLON-EDIT-SRS-19, MELLON-EDIT-SRS-27, MELLON-EDIT-SRS-61, MELLON-EDIT-SRS-63 to -66; mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:486-523 (_write_manifest), mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py:1253-1272
findings.path: create_document(attr_schema=...) writes each entry as given: no name pattern, kind, duplicate, option or required-type check (add_attribute's checks aren't reused). The service then reloads, and a manifest that doesn't load raises LOAD after the folder was written.
findings.impact: An agent's create_document can (1) report failure yet leave a document folder whose manifest doesn't load (kind 'number', or an enumeration without options), so a retry is refused as AlreadyExists; (2) define two attributes with one name, or a text attribute with options; (3) make an attribute required from "required": "false"; (4) declare one parent twice.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section a): kind 'number' -> refused (LOAD) but A1 exists and fails to load; [x:text, x:integer] accepted; enum without options -> refused (LOAD) and A3 left behind; text with options accepted; required 'false' -> required True; parents ['A1','A1'] -> ('A1','A1').
findings.fix: Validate every attr_schema entry with add_attribute's checks (and the parents with add_parent's) before mkdir; treat 'required' as a JSON boolean only.

findings.path: Both patterns are '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' used with re.match. In Python '$' also matches before a final newline, so 'status\n' and 'B1\n' pass.
findings.impact: add_attribute/define_attribute accept the name 'status\n' and write it to the manifest (a name views, rules and filters can't sensibly refer to). create_document('B1\n') fails only because Windows refuses the folder name; on Linux or macOS it creates a folder whose name ends in a newline.
findings.proof:
probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section b): add_attribute 'status
' ACCEPTED, A6 attributes ['type', 'rationale', 'status
']; create_document 'B1
' refused only with WinError 123 (IO). Non-Windows behaviour: analysis.
findings.fix: Use re.fullmatch (or '\Z'), as schema.is_document_id already does; same for the GUI dialogs' copies of the patterns.

findings.path: define_attribute with default_value: the kind check runs, but not the XML text check; editor.add_attribute writes the definition in its own journal; then each set_attribute runs separately and the first one refuses the control character.
findings.impact: The call returns ok=false (error_type OSError, 'backfill ... failed') while the attribute is already defined and no object has the value. A retry is refused as AlreadyExists, so the agent must delete the attribute first.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section c): add_attribute owner default 'a\x01b' -> refused (IO); C attributes now ['type', 'rationale', 'owner']; owner values {'C-0': None, 'C-1': None}.
findings.fix: Check the default with _validate_xml_text before writing, and run the definition plus the backfill in one rollback journal (editor.journal()) so a failure leaves nothing.

findings.path: The backfill loop skips each object whose value for the new attribute isn't empty (`if fresh.objects[obj_id].attrs.get(name, "") != "": continue`).
findings.impact: MELLON-EDIT-SRS-69 (Implemented, 'built as written') says the default goes on each object; the code keeps a value left by a hand edit or another branch, which is half of Proposed MELLON-EDIT-SRS-70 (it doesn't skip objects a rule forbids the attribute on). The requirement and its status note don't describe what 0.3.0 does.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section d): C-1 holds phase='old' by hand; add_attribute phase default 'new' backfills only ['C-0']; values {'C-0': 'new', 'C-1': 'old'}.
findings.fix: Decide: reword MELLON-EDIT-SRS-69 to the built behaviour (or mark SRS-70 partly built), or change the code; either way the test case should cover an object that already holds a value.

findings.path: copy_object creates each copy with editor.create_object, then copies attribute values one set_attribute at a time. A source value set_attribute refuses (an enumeration value that is no longer exactly an option, an attribute the manifest no longer defines; both reach the files by hand edit, merge or option removal) raises after the copy exists. Nothing is checked before the first write and nothing is rolled back.
findings.impact: The agent gets ok=false, error_type 'OSError' and 'stopped after 0 successful copies', but a copy with the description and none of the attribute values is left in the document, not listed in new_ids.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section e): source E-0 status 'approved' (hand edit) -> copy_object refused (IO); objects before ['E-0'], after ['E-0', 'E-1'] with E-1 description 'source', attrs {}.
findings.fix: Validate the source's values (and links) before creating any copy, copy each object's file content in one write, and run the whole call in one rollback journal; report VALIDATION, not IO, for a refused value.

findings.where: MELLON-EDIT-SRS-12 (with Proposed MELLON-EDIT-SRS-11, -37, -72 and MELLON-CHECK-SRS-21, -42); mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py:785-793 (_validate_value_for_attr), mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:808-815 (set_metadata)
findings.path: The composite tools' pre-check and define_attribute's default check say they mirror validation, but test a date with date.fromisoformat, which in Python 3.12 also takes 20261113 and 2026-W46-5. set_metadata does the same. Validation and the GUI editors use validator.is_date (YYYY-MM-DD only).
findings.impact: new_object/update_object/bulk_set_attribute/define_attribute(default) and edit_metadata accept a date that validation then reports (ATTR_BAD_DATE, META_BAD_DATE), so an agent's 'accepted' write fails the gate; the GUI refuses the same value.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p3_date_check_differs.py: update_object due='20261113' and '2026-W46-5' accepted; define_attribute default '20260101' accepted and backfilled; set_metadata date '2026-W46-5' accepted; validate_document then reports META_BAD_DATE and two ATTR_BAD_DATE.
findings.fix: Call validator.value_fits / is_date from the service and set_metadata instead of re-implementing the kind check.

findings.path: max_results is used as hits[:max_results] with no lower bound.
findings.impact: max_results=-1 returns every hit but the last (thousands on a large repository), -5 drops the last five, and 0 returns nothing, which an agent reads as 'no match'.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section f): 5 objects match 'brake'; max_results=-1 -> 4 hits, max_results=0 -> 0 hits.
findings.fix: Refuse max_results below 1 (and above a cap) at the tool.

findings.path: Every data file goes through _write_tree (temp file + os.replace), but a figure is written with shutil.copyfile(src, dest) straight over the existing figures/<id>.svg. copy_object's figure copy isn't even recorded in the journal (no _touch).
findings.impact: If Mellon stops or the disk fills during the copy, the object's existing figure is left truncated: replacing a figure can destroy the old one. The journal puts it back only when an exception is raised in-process.
findings.proof: analysis: shutil.copyfile opens dest for writing (truncating it) and copies in chunks; nothing writes to a temp name first. Unconfirmed by probe (needs a kill or a full disk mid-copy).
findings.fix: Copy to a temp sibling and os.replace it, as _write_tree does (editor._replace_file), and _touch the destination in copy_object.

findings.where: MELLON-EDIT-SRS-1, MELLON-EDIT-SRS-2, MELLON-EDIT-SRS-4; mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:418-435 (create_object), every manifest read-modify-write in editor.py
findings.path: Each editor function reads the manifest, changes it in memory and writes it back, with no lock and no check that the file is unchanged since the read. The GUI checks the disk before a write (check_before_write), but not atomically with it, and the MCP server doesn't check at all.
findings.impact: When an agent and the GUI (or two agents) edit one document at the same moment, one write can drop the other's outline ref, attribute or next object number; two creates that both pass obj_path.exists() write one object file under one ID.
findings.proof: analysis: race between load_document()/etree.parse and _write_tree in two processes; not reproduced. Proposed MELLON-STORE-SRS-182 would refuse the second write.
findings.fix: Compare the manifest's bytes read at the start with the bytes on disk just before os.replace (or take a lock file under .git) and refuse on a mismatch.

findings.path: keep-ancestors calls doc.outline_path(obj_id) for each matched object, and each call walks the outline from the top, so evaluate is quadratic in the document size; the grid re-evaluates the active filter after every cell edit.
findings.impact: Each edit in a large filtered document stalls the GUI: about 0.8 s at 4,000 objects on this machine, and four times as much for each doubling.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p8_filter_ancestors_time.py: 1,000 objects 0.05 s, 2,000 0.19 s, 4,000 0.79 s.
findings.fix: Build a parent map once per evaluate (one outline walk) and climb it per match.

findings.path: set_outline assumes each entry is a dict and 'children' a list: a string entry or children='x' raises AttributeError, which the service doesn't catch (it maps only EditorError, LoaderError, ValueError, OSError).
findings.impact: reorder_outline answers a malformed outline with an internal error ("'str' object has no attribute 'get'") instead of a refusal naming the bad entry. No file is written.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/edit/p7_inputs.py section g): set_outline with children='x', and with a list of id strings -> UNEXPECTED AttributeError.
findings.fix: Check each entry's type in collect() and raise EditorError.

findings.path: The loop tries base x sub for base in (ProgramFiles, LOCALAPPDATA) and sub in (draw.io, Programs/draw.io): four places, %ProgramFiles%\Programs\draw.io and %LOCALAPPDATA%\draw.io among them.
findings.impact: The requirement names two install folders; the code also runs a draw.io.exe found in two others, the second before the per-user install. Harmless for the standard installers, but the documented search order isn't what runs.
findings.proof: analysis: lines 348-354; with draw.io.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\draw.io and in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\draw.io, the first is returned.
findings.fix: Pair each base with its own sub folder, or add the two places to the requirement.

findings.path: A description holds a no-break space U+00A0 (or U+2028/U+2029), as text pasted from Word or written by an agent through MCP does. (a) The user opens the grid's description editor and closes it with Ctrl+Enter without typing: MultiLineTextDelegate.setModelData passes QTextEdit.toPlainText(), which turns U+00A0 into a space, so ObjectsGridModel.setData's equality test (line 306) fails and set_description writes. (b) The user only selects the object (editing enabled) and runs any action (Validate, New, F5, Export...): flush_pending_edits -> Inspector.commit_pending -> _commit_description compares toPlainText() with the stored text (line 534-535), finds a difference and writes.
findings.impact: Text nobody edited is changed on disk: the no-break space becomes a space, the object shows as uncommitted, an undo step 'set description' appears, and the next commit records a change the user never made. In (b) it happens without the user touching the text at all, on every action.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p3_nbsp_rewrite.py prints '(a) file changed after open + Ctrl+Enter with no typing: True', '(a) stored description now has U+00A0: False', '(b) file changed after select + Validate: True'.
findings.fix: Compare with what the editor held when it opened, not with the stored text: keep baseline = editor.toPlainText() right after setEditorData / Inspector._populate_description and write nothing while the text equals it. Better, read the editor with document().toRawText() and map only U+2029 to LF, so no-break spaces survive real edits too. Add a test with U+00A0 and U+2028 in a description for each text field (also the table-cell editor, inline_table._CellDelegate.setModelData).

findings.where: MELLON-GUI-SRS-108; MELLON-GUI-SRS-96; MELLON-GUI-SRS-109; MELLON-GUI-SRS-111 (and Proposed MELLON-GUI-SRS-50); mellon/src/mellon/gui/project_explorer_window.py:378; mellon/src/mellon/gui/controller.py:364; mellon/src/mellon/gui/models/objects_grid.py:264; mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:421; mellon/src/mellon/gui/project_explorer_window.py:325,338
findings.path: All windows share one DocumentService cache, and each Document Editor displays that cache live (ObjectsGridModel._document, Inspector via object_view), while its Changed-on-disk snapshot is taken separately from disk. (A) Editors X and Y are open; an agent changes X-0's status and description; the user presses F5 in Y (or Refresh / activation after a document folder was added in the Project Explorer): invalidate_all() empties the shared cache, and X's grid re-reads X from disk on the next paint. (B) The Project Explorer lists (caches) the documents; an agent changes X-0's description; the user opens X: _open_document uses the cached copy, select_document then snapshots the disk as it is now, so the window shows the old text, activation finds no change, and an edit of the old text passes the write check.
findings.impact: (A) Window X shows part of an external change without a reload and without the banner: X-0's row shows the agent's status beside the old description. (B) A window shows an old copy with no banner, and the user's edit silently overwrites the agent's newer text, the lost update the Changed on disk check exists to stop.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p2_shared_cache.py prints 'X grid status = approved-by-agent', 'X grid description = First requirement', 'banner shown = False' (A) and 'grid description = First requirement', 'banner shown = False', 'user edit of the old text accepted = True', "agent's text still on disk = False" (B).
findings.fix: Make the window's copy and its snapshot come from one read: in _open_document invalidate the document (and its parents) and load them from disk before building the window, and take the snapshot from the digests of the files that load read. Let each Document Editor render its own copy (ObjectsGridModel._shown_doc, the Inspector's view) until it reloads, instead of the shared cache, or give each window its own cache so another window's F5 can't change what it shows.

findings.path: OutlinePane connects only QTreeView.clicked to select_object. The user moves through the outline with the arrow keys (or Home/End/PgDn): the outline's current item moves, but the controller, the grid and the Inspector stay on the object selected before.
findings.impact: The outline highlights one object while the window's selected object is another; Delete, Alt+Up/Down, Indent, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+L then act on the object the outline doesn't highlight.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p1_outline_keyboard.py prints 'after Down: outline current (highlighted) = X-1', 'grid current row object = X-0', 'controller selected object = X-0', 'Inspector shows = X-0'.
findings.fix: Connect outline_view.selectionModel().currentChanged (not clicked) to select_object, guarding against the echo from _on_external_selection as GridPane._on_row_changed does.

findings.where: Proposed MELLON-GUI-SRS-122 (no built requirement covers it); mellon/src/mellon/gui/panels/inspector.py:237; mellon/src/mellon/gui/panels/inspector.py:312-316; mellon/src/mellon/gui/panels/inspector.py:257; mellon/src/mellon/gui/app.py:92-96; mellon/src/mellon/gui/project_explorer_window.py:437-443
findings.path: Text from the repository reaches Qt widgets that interpret HTML: read-only Inspector attribute values are QLabel(value) with Qt's AutoText; outgoing-link rows interpolate link.type, target-doc and target-id unescaped into a RichText label; the form's row labels come from manifest labels; message boxes show load errors and exception text with AutoText. A teammate's commit sets an attribute value (or a link type, which the loader accepts as any string) to .
findings.impact: Merely selecting the object, in the read-only mode every window opens in, makes the GUI open the file the repository text names. With \\host\share\x.png Windows connects to that host and sends the user's NTLM credentials (analysis); other markup can hide or fake text in the Inspector.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p4_richtext.py prints 'value label text format is AutoText: True', 'label size hint: 400 x 300 | same text as plain text: 948 x 12' (the label loaded the 400x300 PNG the value names) and 'outgoing-link labels taller than the image: 1'. The network-path consequence is analysis.
findings.fix: setTextFormat(Qt.PlainText) on every QLabel and QMessageBox that shows repository or git text; html.escape the link fields in the rich link row (or build the row from two plain labels); then build MELLON-GUI-SRS-122.
findings.status: fixed on branch fix/security, 2026-11-14: kept out of this file until fixed because it is a security finding; see docs/open-questions.md Q20

findings.path: Editing enabled, an object with an enumeration or boolean attribute selected. The user turns the mouse wheel while the pointer passes over the Inspector's list (QComboBox), without clicking it: Qt's QComboBox changes its current index on a wheel event even without focus, currentIndexChanged fires, and _commit_attr writes the new value.
findings.impact: A value nobody picked is written to the working copy (high -> low in the probe), with no dialog; the user may only notice it in the next commit's diff.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p11_misc.py prints '(a) combo has focus before wheel: False', '(a) file changed by a wheel turn over the Inspector's list: True', '(a) priority on disk now: low'.
findings.fix: Save on QComboBox.activated (a user pick) instead of currentIndexChanged, and give the list Qt.StrongFocus with an event filter that ignores wheel events unless it has the focus. The grid's enumeration editor (AttrDelegate) already saves on activated.

findings.path: A background job catches an unexpected exception and only emits it to the window ('crashed'), whose slot re-raises it into the excepthook. The user starts an export and closes the Document Editor (or closes the Compare dialog mid-compare) before the job fails: the signal has no receiver left (export) or emitting raises RuntimeError, which _emit swallows (compare).
findings.impact: An unexpected error in an export or comparison is neither logged nor shown, so a defect in the exporter leaves no trace; this is the case the requirement's rationale asks to test.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p5_export_crash_log.py (exporter replaced by one that raises ZeroDivisionError) prints 'window kept open : error logged = True' and 'window closed    : error logged = False'. The compare path is analysis (same pattern).
findings.fix: Write the exception to the error log in the job itself (call sys.excepthook or a shared log function from run(), which already logs without a dialog off the GUI thread), and keep the GUI-thread re-raise only for the dialog.

findings.where: MELLON-GUI-SRS-117 (Proposed MELLON-VER-SRS-186 would settle it); mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:238
findings.path: The Document Editor refreshes its git cell on activation, commit and edit_succeeded (field edits) only. New sibling/child, Move, Indent, Delete, Link, Ack, figure and table actions, Undo and Redo write files without refreshing it.
findings.impact: After the user's own New sibling the bar still shows no uncommitted change while two files are uncommitted, until the window is re-activated; a user who checks the bar before switching to the git client is misled. Whether 'shall show the number' includes when it is updated isn't stated.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p6_status_inspector.py prints "after New sibling   status bar: 'master @ bba15a3'   actual uncommitted files: 2" (same after Move down and Undo).
findings.fix: Refresh the git cell from the service change listener (_on_files_changed) and after Undo/Redo and Discard; accept MELLON-VER-SRS-186 to fix the timing.

findings.path: uncommitted_document_paths raises (git status fails: unreadable or locked index, a corrupt repository, a permission problem): both windows catch every Exception and set n = 0.
findings.impact: The status bar then shows no count and its tooltip says 'no uncommitted document changes': a failure reads as a clean working copy.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p11_misc.py prints "(c) listing fails -> status bar: 'master @ ...' | tooltip: 'no uncommitted document changes'".
findings.fix: Show that the count is unavailable (for example '? uncommitted' with the error in the tooltip), and catch ServiceError only, so other errors reach the error log.

findings.path: A repository with no commit yet (a new repository, MELLON-STORE-SRS-13) on branch main: repo.head raises for an unborn HEAD, head_summary returns (None, None), and the bar shows '(no commits)'.
findings.impact: The bar doesn't name the branch the first commit will go on. With no latest commit the requirement's hash can't be shown, but the branch can.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p11_misc.py prints "(d) no commit yet, branch 'main' checked out -> status bar: '(no commits) · 2 dirty'".
findings.fix: Read the branch from the symbolic HEAD (repo.references['HEAD'].target) when HEAD is unborn and show 'main (no commits)'; say in MELLON-GUI-SRS-115 what an unborn branch shows.

findings.path: Each window builds its own Theme submenu and checks the current choice once, when built. The user picks Light in a Document Editor.
findings.impact: The theme is applied to every window, but the Project Explorer's and other editors' Theme menus still show the previous choice checked.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p11_misc.py prints "(b) chosen: light | editor menu checked: ['light'] | Project Explorer menu checked: ['dark']".
findings.fix: Connect ThemeManager.theme_changed (or a choice_changed signal) to update each window's actions.

findings.path: Under the Changed on disk banner (1) the Inspector's fields are made read-only or disabled, so typing into the description or an attribute, or opening a list, does nothing and shows no message; (2) Discard uncommitted changes is allowed on purpose (docstring), and discard_document_changes isn't a checked write, so it overwrites the external change the window hasn't shown yet.
findings.impact: (1) The grid says 'Changed on disk. Reload first (F5).' for the same input, the Inspector says nothing (only the banner is there). (2) A user who discards to drop their own edits also throws away an agent's uncommitted work in the document, which the window never displayed. Whether a field locked silently counts as refusing 'with a message', and whether Discard is an edit under -104, isn't stated.
findings.proof: analysis: Inspector._lock_fields_while_stale calls setReadOnly/setEnabled(False) and no path emits edit_failed for typing; _discard_document_changes runs svc.discard_document_changes, which has no writes_files marker, so _EditorService doesn't check the disk.
findings.fix: Decide both in the SRS. If -104 covers them: show the stale message when a locked Inspector field is clicked or typed into, and ask again (naming the external change) or refuse Discard under the banner.

findings.path: Inspector._populate_attrs iterates over the object's own attrs, so an attribute the manifest defines but the object doesn't set gets no row. In the probe the manifest defines type, rationale, status and priority, X-0 sets only status, and validation reports 'required attribute type is missing'.
findings.impact: The Inspector shows one of four attributes; the '* label' mark for a required attribute without a value never appears for an unset one, and such an attribute can't be set from the Inspector (only from a grid column, if shown). 'The selected object's attributes' can mean the set ones or every defined one.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p6_status_inspector.py prints "manifest attributes: ['type', 'rationale', 'status', 'priority']", "X-0 attrs on disk  : {'status': 'draft'}", "Inspector rows     : ['status:']".
findings.fix: Say in -55 which attributes are shown; if every defined one, iterate over doc.attributes (plus any set attribute the manifest lacks) and show unset ones empty, marked required where a rule requires them.

findings.path: Undo and Redo take Qt's platform key bindings (QKeySequence.StandardKey). On Windows Redo is Ctrl+Y, Alt+Shift+Backspace, Ctrl+Shift+Z; on KDE and GNOME Qt's table gives Redo as Ctrl+Shift+Z only.
findings.impact: On Linux, Ctrl+Y doesn't run Redo, which -163 requires without naming a platform; on Windows Alt+Backspace and Alt+Shift+Backspace also undo and redo, which no requirement lists. The Close action already sets explicit keys for this reason (comment at line 483).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p9_shortcuts.py prints "Redo keys: ['Ctrl+Y', 'Alt+Shift+Backspace', 'Ctrl+Shift+Z', 'Redo']" on Windows. The Linux bindings are analysis from Qt's key-binding table, not run.
findings.fix: Set the keys explicitly ([Ctrl+Z] and [Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+Shift+Z]), or say in the SRS that these keys are Windows keys.

findings.path: argparse's version action writes to sys.stdout and exits 0. In a windowed build with no console, sys.stdout is None and argparse silently writes nothing.
findings.impact: If the frozen mellon.exe has no stdout even when its output is redirected, mellon.exe --version exits 0 and prints nothing, so -8 isn't met by the installed GUI and the release smoke test (exit status only, per -7) can't notice.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p8_version_log.py prints "--version: exit 0 | stdout 'mellon-gui 0.3.0\n'" and, with sys.stdout = None, 'exit code 0 | bytes written anywhere: none'. Whether the frozen exe's stdout is None is decided by packaging, not in the checkout.
findings.fix: Check mellon.exe --version > v.txt on the released build; if empty, write the number with os.write(1, ...) when sys.stdout is None, or attach a console for --version.

findings.path: The excepthook is installed in main() after every GUI module has been imported (app.py lines 25-28) and after QApplication is created. An ImportError (a module a frozen build left out), or a failure while creating QApplication or setting its names, happens before it.
findings.impact: In the windowed mellon.exe such an error goes to sys.stderr, which is None, so the program ends with no window and no log entry.
findings.proof: analysis: order of statements in app.py; the frozen entry script (packaging/launch_gui.py) isn't in the checkout and may install its own hook, so this is unconfirmed.
findings.fix: Install a minimal hook (log path computed from %LOCALAPPDATA% without Qt) at the top of the entry point before importing the GUI modules.

findings.path: Every write in a Document Editor appends an undo step that keeps the full bytes of each file before and after (Journal.before/after). Structural edits (New, Move, Indent, Delete) rewrite the manifest, whose size grows with the number of objects. Steps are dropped only at a commit, a reload or the banner.
findings.impact: A long session of reorganising a large document without committing grows memory without limit (two manifest copies per Move); nothing tells the user.
findings.proof: analysis: _on_files_changed appends (label, changes) with no limit; Journal.seal stores the after bytes of every file; EDIT-SRS-349 requires every step since the latest commit to be kept.
findings.fix: Bound the history (by bytes or steps, dropping the oldest and saying so), or keep step bytes on disk outside the repository; add the bound to the SRS.

findings.where: Proposed MELLON-GUI-SRS-3, -15, -59, -60, -62, -128 (rationales say 'Implemented if 0.3.0 does this')
findings.path: Behaviour of the code under review against these Proposed requirements: -3 open_repo skips the root check for a missing path and the load raises 'cannot read repo root <path>', shown in a warning with no repository open; -15 closing by Ctrl+W, or opening another repository, saved typed grid and Inspector text (focus-out on close); -59 _indent/_outdent/_move_up/_move_down end with select_object(doc_id, sel); -60 _new_sibling/_new_child/_new_top_level select new_id; -62 reload_document re-selects the current object if it still exists; -128 load_choice defaults to 'system'.
findings.impact: These may be set to Implemented once their tests exist; -35 (empty repository message) is not met: the list is just empty.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/gui/p7_close_pending.py prints '(a) grid text saved on Ctrl+W: True', '(b) Inspector text saved on Ctrl+W: True', '(c) grid text saved when another repository opened: True' (offscreen platform); the rest is analysis of controller.py:282-296, main_window.py:1045,1064,1104, controller.py:389-392, theme.py:402.
findings.fix: Confirm on the released build and update the statuses through the process.

findings.where: MELLON-MCP-SRS-53; mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py: remove_link, clear_figure, clear_table, remove_parent_doc
findings.path: remove_link on a link that doesn't exist, clear_figure on an object with no figure, clear_table on an object with no table, remove_parent_doc for a parent that isn't declared: each tool builds its own failure dict with "error_type": "NotFound" instead of going through _ERROR_TYPE_BY_CODE.
findings.impact: A write call whose parameters name a missing item returns error_type NotFound, which no requirement lists, where MELLON-MCP-SRS-53 says EditorError. An agent branching on EditorError for 'my input named something that isn't there' misses these four tools. delete_object blocked by incoming links likewise returns the ad-hoc BlockedByIncomingLinks.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p3_results.py prints: remove_link that doesn't exist ... error_type 'NotFound'; clear_figure with no figure ... 'NotFound'; clear_table with no table ... 'NotFound'; remove_parent_doc not declared ... 'NotFound'.
findings.fix: Return error_type EditorError for these four (use _service_error_result with ServiceError(ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, ...)). This needs a person's decision first: 0.3.0 already returns NotFound, and MELLON-MCP-SRS-38 asks that a released error_type value stays, so either the change is recorded in the changelog as a break, or NotFound goes into MELLON-MCP-SRS-55's table and MELLON-MCP-SRS-53 is reworded. Either way, not in code alone.

findings.path: update_object(add_links=[a link that already exists]) raises ServiceError(VALIDATION, 'link already exists ...'); new_object or update_object with the same target twice in links/add_links raises ServiceError(VALIDATION, 'duplicate link in request ...'). Both map to EditorError.
findings.impact: Asking to add a second link from one source to one target returns AlreadyExists through add_link but EditorError through update_object and new_object, so an agent that treats AlreadyExists as 'already done, carry on' fails the same request depending on the tool it used.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p3_results.py prints: add_link B0->A0 again ... 'AlreadyExists'; update_object add_links B0->A0 (exists) ... 'EditorError', 'link already exists: B-0 -> A/A-0'; new_object with one target twice ... 'EditorError'.
findings.fix: Raise ServiceError(ErrorCode.ALREADY_EXISTS, ...) for both cases in update_object and _validate_composite_links.

findings.path: create_document(doc_id='C', attr_schema=[{'kind': 'enum'}]) (an entry without a name): editor.create_document writes C/C.xml and C/objects/, then DocumentService.create_document's self._reload(doc_id) raises LoaderError, which propagates as ServiceError(LOAD).
findings.impact: The call returns ok false, error_type LoaderError and affected_files [] but leaves a new document folder behind whose manifest doesn't load. A retry gets AlreadyExists, validate_repo and every repository-wide answer now report a load error for C, and nothing tells the agent which files to remove. The refused value is the agent's to fix, which MELLON-MCP-SRS-53 gives EditorError.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p4_commit_fail.py prints: isError=False ok=False error_type=LoaderError affected_files=[]; files created by the failed call: ['C/C.xml']; retry create_document C: False AlreadyExists; validate_repo ok: False load_errors: ['C'].
findings.fix: Check each attr_schema entry (name, kind, options) before writing anything, as define_attribute does, and refuse with EditorError; and run the reload inside the editor's rollback journal so that any failure after the first write removes the folder again.

findings.where: MELLON-MCP-SRS-45, MELLON-MCP-SRS-91; mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py: _refusing_tool, _auto_commit_if_requested; mellon/src/mellon/git_ops.py: commit; mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py: DocumentService._validate_composite_links
findings.path: (1) new_object or update_object with a link entry whose target_doc is a list or object passes the schema (list[dict]) and then `target_doc not in allowed` raises TypeError, which _refusing_tool doesn't catch. (2) In git_ops.commit, pygit2's index.add raises OSError for an operating-system error (here 'could not find ... to stat'); the handler catches only pygit2.GitError, DocumentService.commit only GitError and _auto_commit_if_requested only ServiceError.
findings.impact: (1) A failed write tool call comes back as a protocol tool error with plain text, not ok false, error and error_type, so an agent that reads the result shape can't tell what happened. (2) The same escape in the commit after a successful write would report the whole call as an error with no commit_error, although the files were written; the agent retries and a repeated new_object makes a second object.
findings.proof: (1) probe codeview-probe/mcp/p3_results.py prints: new_object link target_doc a list: isError=True Error executing tool new_object: unhashable type: 'list'. (2) probe codeview-probe/mcp/p6_paths.py prints for commit_changes with an absolute path: isError=True ... could not find '...' to stat, an OSError from index.add escaping git_ops.commit; that a write tool's commit meets the same escape is analysis: _auto_commit_if_requested calls the same DocumentService.commit, and affected_files can name a file another program removes or locks between the write and the commit (unconfirmed).
findings.fix: Catch OSError (and ValueError) from index.add, write_tree and index.write in git_ops.commit and raise GitError naming the path; in _auto_commit_if_requested catch Exception and return commit_error; give _write_tool a last-resort except Exception that returns ok false with the error_type MELLON-MCP-SRS-56 will fix; check that target_doc and target_id are strings in _validate_composite_links.

findings.path: A commit whose selected file is byte-range locked by another program: pygit2 raises GitError with the message 'no error', which git_ops.commit passes on unchanged.
findings.impact: The agent gets a commit failure whose reason reads 'no error', so neither it nor the person can tell that a locked file stopped the commit or which file it was.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p4_commit_fail.py (case 2, commit_changes naming a locked object file) prints: ok False, error 'no error', error_type 'GitError'. For a write tool's commit_message the same DocumentService.commit is used (analysis).
findings.fix: When pygit2's message is empty or 'no error', raise GitError naming the path being added and the likely cause (a file held open by another program).

findings.where: MELLON-MCP-SRS-67; mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py: ack_suspects, set_attribute, change_attribute_required, move_object
findings.path: (1) ack_suspects builds affected_files with one entry per acknowledged link, so two links from one object list B/links/B-0.xml twice. (2) set_attribute with the value already stored, change_attribute_required with the current flag and move_object to the place the object already has list a file whose bytes don't change: the lists are built from what the tool was asked to do, not from what changed.
findings.impact: affected_files isn't 'exactly' the changed files: a duplicate entry, or a file that didn't change. With commit_message, the unchanged case returns ok true plus commit_error 'nothing to commit', which reads as a failure of a call that did nothing wrong.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p3_results.py prints: ack_suspects B (two links, one source): listed=['B/links/B-0.xml', 'B/links/B-0.xml'] changed=['B/links/B-0.xml'] DUPLICATES; set_attribute same value again + commit_message: listed=['A/objects/A-0.xml'] changed=[] MISMATCH commit_error={'error': 'nothing to commit (no changes staged)'}; change_attribute_required to same value: listed=['A/A.xml'] changed=[] MISMATCH; move_object to where it is: listed=['A/A.xml'] changed=[] MISMATCH.
findings.fix: Build affected_files from the editor journal that DocumentService._recorded already opens (each file's bytes before and after), keeping only files whose bytes differ, de-duplicated; or at least de-duplicate in ack_suspects.

findings.where: MELLON-MCP-SRS-2; mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py: git_history, show_object_at, inspect_object, review_suspect_link; mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py: DocumentService.current_issue, DocumentService.tag_issue; mellon/src/mellon/suspects.py: scan_document
findings.path: These open the repository with discover_repo(<root>/<doc_id>), which walks up from the document folder. If the document folder holds a repository of its own (a submodule, or a clone put there), they use that one, not the folder to serve.
findings.impact: git_history reports 'No object' for an object that exists and is committed in the served repository; tag_issue puts the issue tag in the inner repository, and current_issue then reports it, while the served repository has no tag. suspects.scan_document uses the same call, so link states would come from the inner history too (not probed).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p5_race_nested.py (b) prints: git_history ... isError=True "No object 'A-0' in document 'A'"; tag_issue: True created tag A-issue-1; served repo tags=[]; nested repo tags=['refs/tags/A-issue-1']; show_document current_issue='1'.
findings.fix: Open the repository once from the folder to serve (pygit2.Repository(_State.repo_root)) and pass it down, instead of discovering from each document folder; or refuse a document folder that holds .git.

findings.path: git_history builds f"{doc_id}/objects/{obj_id}.xml" and calls (root / rel).exists() before checking obj_id; commit_changes' paths go to _selected_files, which stats root / rel for a '../' path before libgit2 refuses it.
findings.impact: An obj_id or path with '../' makes the server look at files outside the repository, and the answer differs on whether the file exists: an existence check on any *.xml file (git_history) or any file (commit_changes) the person can read, steerable by repository text. MELLON-MCP-SRS-112 allows only source_path and out_path outside.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p6_paths.py prints: git_history obj_id='../../../<x>-outside' (existing file outside): isError=False '' versus (missing file outside): "No object ..."; commit_changes paths=['../<x>-outside.xml'] (existing): error "invalid path" versus (missing): 'nothing to commit (no changes staged)'.
findings.fix: In git_history check is_object_id(doc_id, obj_id) (or that the object is in the document) before building a path; in _selected_files refuse an absolute path or one with a '..' part before touching the disk.
findings.status: fixed on branch fix/security, 2026-11-14: kept out of this file until fixed because it is a security finding; see docs/open-questions.md Q20

findings.path: A misspelt option (--read-onyl) or a refused value (--log-level debug): argparse prints usage and exits with status 2 before any folder is chosen.
findings.impact: MELLON-MCP-SRS-10 reads 'when the MCP server exits with status 2, write the reason and the absolute path of the refused folder'. Status 2 also means a bad option, where no folder is refused and none is written, so a person reading the client's log can't tell 'wrong folder' from 'wrong option' by status, and the requirement can't hold as worded.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p2_start.py prints: misspelt --read-onyl: exit=2 ... 'mellon-mcp: error: unrecognized arguments: --read-onyl'; --log-level debug (lower case): exit=2 ... invalid choice: 'debug'.
findings.fix: Either condition MELLON-MCP-SRS-10 on refusing the folder to serve, or pin MELLON-MCP-SRS-31 to another status and make main() use it (parser.exit / a subclass of ArgumentParser.error).

findings.path: A parsed file is reused while its st_mtime_ns and st_size are unchanged. Another program rewrites an object file with text of the same length and keeps the file's old modified time (a copy that preserves timestamps, a sync client restoring a version, touch -r).
findings.impact: Each later call answers from the old text for as long as the server runs, with no hint that it is stale. The racy-write guard (_RACY_NS) covers a rewrite within the clock tick, not one that keeps the old time.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p9_commit_and_freshness.py prints: a1 before: someone else's draft; a1 after a same-size rewrite that kept its old mtime: someone else's draft (the file holds SOMEONE ELSE'S DRAFT). The racy case is handled: same size + same mtime rewrite, read right after: ONE V2.
findings.fix: Add more of the file's identity to the key: st_ino and, where the platform has it, the change time (st_ctime_ns on POSIX); or drop the reuse for files the working copy shows as modified. Low likelihood; worth a decision.

findings.path: Two overlapping calls run one after the other only because FastMCP 1.27 calls synchronous tool functions on its event loop. Neither the server nor DocumentService holds a lock, and _write_tree's temp name '.{name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp' is the same for two calls in one process.
findings.impact: Today the property holds. If the MCP library starts running synchronous tools in worker threads (a change other frameworks have made, and mcp 2.x is a rewrite), overlapping writes interleave, two writes to one file share a temp file, and next-object-number races, with nothing in Mellon's code to catch it.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/mcp/p1_overlap.py prints: two calls took 1.03s; peak concurrent = 1; new ids: ['D-0', 'D-1', 'D-2', 'D-3']. The risk on a library change is analysis (unconfirmed).
findings.fix: Hold one module-level threading.Lock around every tool body (a decorator applied with @mcp.tool()), so the property is Mellon's and not the library's; say so in a comment naming MELLON-MCP-SRS-105.

findings.where: MELLON-MCP-SRS-55 (Proposed), MELLON-MCP-SRS-56 (Proposed); mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py: _ERROR_TYPE_BY_CODE, clear_figure, clear_table, remove_parent_doc, remove_link, delete_object, _auto_commit_if_requested
findings.path: Checked the error_type values the server can return against MELLON-MCP-SRS-55's table (AlreadyExists, EditorError, OSError, PermissionError, TectonicError, and three TBD rows). Outside the table: NotFound (clear_figure, clear_table, remove_parent_doc, remove_link), BlockedByIncomingLinks (delete_object without force), LoaderError (ErrorCode.LOAD: a write to a document that doesn't load, or create_document's failed reload) and GitError (ErrorCode.GIT: tag_issue on a tag conflict, ack_suspects without git, commit_changes, and commit_error.error_type). Unreachable but present: 'ServiceError' as the fallback in _service_error_result and in commit_error, and 'Refusal' as _Refusal.error_type.
findings.impact: With MELLON-MCP-SRS-55 as written, 0.3.0 returns four values the table doesn't list, so the requirement fails as soon as it is accepted. LoaderError and GitError are two values where MELLON-MCP-SRS-56 asks for one fixed value for everything no other row covers, and NotFound clashes with MELLON-MCP-SRS-53 (see that finding).
findings.proof: probes: codeview-probe/mcp/p3_results.py prints error_type 'NotFound' (four tools), 'BlockedByIncomingLinks', and commit_error error_type 'GitError'; codeview-probe/mcp/p4_commit_fail.py prints error_type LoaderError (create_document) and 'GitError' (commit_changes). 'ServiceError' and 'Refusal' are analysis: every ErrorCode has a mapping and nothing raises _Refusal itself.
findings.fix: Decide per value (a person's call, as MELLON-MCP-SRS-38 makes each one released interface): add NotFound and BlockedByIncomingLinks as rows or map them to EditorError; fill the TBD of MELLON-MCP-SRS-56 with one value and map LoaderError and GitError to it or give them rows of their own; then remove the 'ServiceError' and 'Refusal' literals so the set in code is the table.

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-119, MELLON-PDF-SRS-122; mellon/src/mellon/templates/syrs/main.tex.j2:45-52 (the `elif it.obj.table is not none` branch)

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-135; mellon/src/mellon/export.py:40-68 (escape_latex), mellon/src/mellon/templates/syrs/syrs.cls:19-35 (fonts loaded through fontspec with its default TeX input mapping)
findings.path: A description 'Shift x >> 2 and y << 3; Vec<Vec<u8>> ok; a,,b; wow!`x; q?`y'. escape_latex leaves > < , ! ? alone, and XeTeX's tex-text mapping turns the pairs into single characters.
findings.impact: The PDF prints 'x » 2', 'y « 3', 'Vec<Vec<u8»', 'a„b', 'wow¡x', 'q¿y': shift operators, generics and doubled commas change into other characters in an issued requirement. The same path prints attribute values, table cells, captions, headings and the cover, and also turns ' into ’, " into ” and -- into an en dash (MELLON-PDF-SRS-136, Proposed).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p1_content.py prints the extracted line 'REQUIREMENT Shift x » 2 and y « 3; Vec<Vec<u8» ok; a„b; wow¡x; q¿y; end.'; p9_cover_misc.py shows each listed character alone prints correctly, so only the pairs fail.
findings.fix: Load the fonts without the TeX input mapping (fontspec Ligatures=TeX / Mapping=tex-text), or have escape_latex break each pair (>{}> , <{}<, ,{}, , !{}`, ?{}`, -{}-) and write ' " ` as \textquotesingle, \textquotedbl, \textasciigrave; test each pair in each field against the PDF's text layer.

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-126; mellon/src/mellon/templates/syrs/syrs.cls:496-514 (\attrs is a fixed five-column tabularx), mellon/src/mellon/templates/syrs/main.tex.j2:65
findings.path: export_document(doc_id, out_path, attrs=[six attribute names]) on an object that has a value for all six. main.tex.j2 joins one \attrcell per value with & into one row of the five-column tabularx.
findings.impact: The export fails ('Extra alignment tab has been changed to \cr'), so an agent that chooses six attributes, for instance type, status, level, req-type, rationale and verification-method for Mellon's own SRS documents, gets no PDF at all. Five work.

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-10, MELLON-PDF-SRS-45, MELLON-PDF-SRS-172; mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:2337-2351 (_export_current_doc), mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py:247-261 (_load returns the cached copy), mellon/src/mellon/service/cache.py:80-86 (suspect scans keyed by HEAD only)
findings.path: Document Editor open in read-only mode; an agent changes DOC-0's description and deletes (uncommitted) the parent object DOC-0 links to; the window is activated, so the Changed on disk banner goes up; Ctrl+E. _export_current_doc reads the document and its parents through the cache (no reload, no stale check), and _link_problems gets the scan cached for the unchanged HEAD.
findings.impact: The PDF prints the window's old copy, not the working copy, with the Changed on disk banner showing; the export warning isn't shown although the link is broken in the working copy; and the Traceability section counts the deleted parent object as covered ('PAR: 1 of 1'). A parent that now has a load error but is still cached is counted the same way instead of being named (SRS-172). The scan cache is TRACE's too (state gutter).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p6_gui_stale.py (offscreen GUI, real export job): banner up True; fresh scan says ('DOC-0', 'broken'); _link_problems returns []; export warning shown False; PDF holds ORIGINALTEXT True, AGENTTEXT False; 'PAR: 1 of 1 objects have a link from this document.'
findings.fix: In _export_current_doc, check the disk first (_changed_on_disk) and refuse while stale, as edits do, or reload; read the document and parents for the job from disk; drop cached suspect scans whenever a document folder changed on disk (they depend on the working copy, not only HEAD).

findings.path: export_document('DOC', '\\?\C:\...\repo\.git\e.pdf'). Path.resolve() keeps the \\?\ prefix, so is_relative_to() compares drive '\\?\C:' with 'C:' and finds no match.
findings.impact: The PDF is written inside the repository's .git folder, which the requirement forbids; an agent steered by repository text can overwrite git's files with a PDF. .GIT, .git., DOC/../.git, a junction to .git and GIT~1 are all refused correctly.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p3_gitpath.py (typesetter stubbed): 'long-path prefix -> ok=True', and .git then holds e.pdf; the six other spellings return ok=False.
findings.fix: Strip the extended-length prefix before comparing (or refuse \\?\ and \\.\ paths, as MELLON-PDF-SRS-31 proposes), and compare by resolved, case-folded paths; add the prefixed spelling to the test.

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-59, MELLON-PDF-SRS-62; mellon/src/mellon/export.py:588-595 (_render_figures swallows DrawioError), mellon/src/mellon/drawio.py:344-346 (find_drawio returns MELLON_DRAWIO unchecked), mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:2405-2413, mellon/src/mellon/mcp/server.py:2583
findings.path: MELLON_DRAWIO names a file that doesn't exist; export a document with figures. find_drawio() returns the setting as found; export_pdfs raises DrawioError ('could not run draw.io'); _render_figures returns {} without the reason; the callers ask find_drawio() again, which is still not None.
findings.impact: Mellon can't find draw.io, yet the MCP result has no drawio_found false and the Document Editor's notice says 'draw.io couldn't render them; an empty figure is one reason', so the user looks for a fault in the figures instead of the setting. A draw.io timeout or crash is reported the same way, its reason dropped.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p4_figures.py (a): find_drawio() returns the missing path; result keys have no drawio_found; message '4 figure(s) not rendered (see unrendered_figures)'. The GUI notice text is from main_window.py:2413 (analysis: same find_drawio() test).
findings.fix: Have _render_figures return why nothing was drawn (not found, couldn't start, timed out with the DrawioError text) and pass it to the notice and the MCP result; treat a MELLON_DRAWIO that names no file as not found (MELLON-EDIT-SRS-248, Proposed).

findings.path: The program run for the export starts child processes that inherit its output pipes, then hangs. subprocess.run(timeout=...) kills only the program it started, then on Windows reads the pipes to the end, which waits for the children.
findings.impact: The export doesn't end at the limit: it waits as long as any child lives, possibly without end, and leaves the children running. draw.io desktop is an Electron program with child processes, and a MELLON_TECTONIC wrapper script behaves like the stand-in. Unconfirmed for real draw.io.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p10_timeout_child.py with .bat stand-ins and the limit patched to 3 s: export_pdfs returned after 59.6 s and _run_tectonic after 59.8 s. proof for draw.io itself: analysis.
findings.fix: Start the program in its own job object (or process group) and end the whole tree at the limit; read output through files or bound the read after the kill; MELLON-PDF-SRS-43 (Proposed) asks the same.

findings.path: Installed build, TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR set in the user's environment (as it is for anyone who also uses tectonic elsewhere), no network. _run_tectonic uses the installer's pre-filled cache only when TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR is unset.
findings.impact: The installed Mellon then needs the network for its export, and fails offline with 'the first PDF export needs internet access', although the requirement says the installed build exports without one. GUI-SRS-184's rationale handed this case to PDF (CF-G64).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p5_offline.py: with every proxy variable on a closed port, the pre-filled cache exports (10 pages); the same export with TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR pointing at an empty folder fails with that message. Not run on a clean machine, and the installer's entry scripts (mellon/packaging, outside this review's reading list) weren't read, so whether they clear the variable is unconfirmed.
findings.fix: In the frozen build, always use the bundled cache (or use TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR only through a Mellon-specific setting); test the installed build with TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR set.

findings.path: The suspect scan raises ServiceError (a GitError from the history walk or link index: a corrupt or missing object, a partial clone). The GUI returns [] and the MCP tool sets problems = [] with the comment 'no git: nothing to check against', although the root check already guarantees git.
findings.impact: The export warning isn't shown and the MCP result has no suspect_links, which reads as 'no suspect or broken links' for a document that may have them; nothing says the states weren't worked out.
findings.proof: analysis: the two except branches quoted; not provoked by a probe.
findings.fix: Report a failed scan: in the GUI show the export warning saying link states couldn't be worked out (the direction of MELLON-PDF-SRS-46, -53), and in the MCP result return a field saying the links weren't checked, with the error.

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-67 (Proposed) and MELLON-EDIT-SRS-247 (Proposed); mellon/src/mellon/export.py:465 (_find_tectonic: shutil.which('tectonic')), mellon/src/mellon/drawio.py:355-358 (find_drawio: shutil.which)
findings.path: No MELLON_TECTONIC, a source or uv tool install, the MCP server started in the repository (its usual working folder), and a tectonic.bat committed to the repository. On Windows, shutil.which searches the current folder first unless NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is set. The same holds for draw.io's PATH fallback (drawio/draw.io .bat/.cmd/.exe) when draw.io isn't in its standard folders, installed build included.
findings.impact: Exporting runs a program from the repository: anyone who can push runs code on the machine of whoever exports. Recorded because the code does this today; the requirements that forbid it are Proposed (decided on 2026-11-11).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p8_cwd_program.py: this agent environment sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 (then nothing is found); with it unset, as on a normal desktop, _find_tectonic() returns '.\tectonic.BAT' and build_pdf runs it (marker written).
findings.fix: Look up programs only in absolute PATH entries outside the repository and the start folder (set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath in os.environ before shutil.which, and skip relative PATH entries), as MELLON-PDF-SRS-67 and MELLON-EDIT-SRS-247 propose.
findings.status: fixed on branch fix/security, 2026-11-14: kept out of this file until fixed because it is a security finding; see docs/open-questions.md Q20

findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-72 (Proposed), MELLON-PDF-SRS-136 (Proposed); mellon/src/mellon/templates/syrs/syrs.cls:19-35 (Latin Modern when Inter isn't installed), mellon/src/mellon/export.py:548-567 (build_pdf checks only the exit status)
findings.path: A description '5 ≤ 6 ≥ 4' (≤ and ≥ are printable characters in definitions.md). The font has no glyph for them; XeTeX logs 'Missing character' and goes on; build_pdf ignores warnings.
findings.impact: The PDF prints '5 6 4' and the export reports success: the requirement's meaning changes silently. Recorded under C13 because the typesetter's warning is swallowed; reporting it is Proposed (SRS-72).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p5_offline.py: 'Δ', 'Ω', 'µ', '“' are in the PDF text, '≤' and '≥' are not.
