findings.where: MELLON-PDF-SRS-65; mellon/src/mellon/export.py:507-512 (_run_tectonic timeout message), mellon/src/mellon/export.py:556-560 (build_pdf error message)
findings.path: The typesetter hits the 300 s limit on a large document with the installer's pre-filled cache, or fails on a TeX error.
findings.impact: The timeout's reason says 'a first export may be downloading TeX files — check the network and try again', wrong for the installed build, where the cause is the document's size (SRS-70's rationale calls it a defect to fix); a TeX error's reason is the typesetter's whole stdout and stderr, shown as is in the Export failed dialog and the MCP error.
findings.proof: analysis: the message strings quoted; the timeout case wasn't run (p7 took 176 s for 1,000 objects).
findings.fix: State the limit and the document size as the reason, and give the network hint only when the cache is incomplete; put the first TeX error line, with its object if known, in the message and the full log in a file.

findings.path: Outline: Heading 'Intro' (1), a top-level Requirement, and under that Requirement a Heading. The heading macro is chosen by outline depth alone, and the LaTeX counters number it after the last section.
findings.impact: The heading under the requirement is numbered 1.2, as if it were under heading 1 (before any top-level heading it would be 0.1; under heading > requirement it is 1.0.1). The requirement only says '1.1, 1.2 under heading 1' and doesn't say how a heading whose parent isn't a heading is numbered.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p1_content.py contents page: '1.1 Heading with table', '1.2 Heading under a requirement', '2 Second heading'.
findings.fix: Decide the rule (number by heading ancestry, as DOORS does) in MELLON-PDF-SRS-115 and test a heading under a requirement.

findings.path: A document titled 'Child spec', exported.
findings.impact: Each page header shows 'CHILD SPEC'. Whether an upper-cased title counts as 'the title' isn't said; a reader searching for the title's text won't match it in headers (MELLON-PDF-SRS-136 would require the title as held).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p1_content.py: header of page 3 ['CHD', 'CHILD SPEC', 'Rev. R7 • 2026-11-13'].
findings.fix: Say whether the header may change the title's letter case, or print it as held.

findings.path: A 1,000-object document (50 headings, 950 requirements of about 30 words with three attributes, each linking to one object of a 1,000-object parent; one commit, not one per object) exported through export_document with the installer's tectonic.
findings.impact: 176 s from the call to the PDF written, above the 150 s limit; a second run of the same document spent 274.9 s in the typesetter alone (load 0.8 s, link scan 0.0 s, LaTeX 0.1 s), 25 s short of the 300 s stop. Other review agents were running probes on the machine, so load wasn't controlled; whether this machine is the reference machine isn't known, and the document's history differs from the reference document's. The typesetter is the whole cost, so the margin to the 300 s stop is thin under load.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/pdf/p7_perf.py (p7_perf.out): 'export_document, 1,000 objects: 176.0 s'; p7b_perf_split.py (p7b_perf_split.out): 'typesetter 274.9 s'.
findings.fix: Measure on the reference machine with the reference document, idle; if 150 s holds only there, say so in the requirement's test case, and look at the typesetter's pass count (contents, LastPage and longtable each need reruns).

findings.path: The comment above render_latex's subject argument: 'MELLON-PDF-SRS-82: no title, no title on the cover or in the header'.
findings.impact: MELLON-PDF-SRS-82 covers the cover page only; leaving the field out of the page header is MELLON-PDF-SRS-83, which is Proposed. The comment names a requirement the code only partly implements.
findings.proof: analysis: compare the comment with the two requirements' text.
findings.fix: Cite MELLON-PDF-SRS-82 for the cover and MELLON-PDF-SRS-83 for the header (or drop the header from the comment).

findings.path: Read against the code under review; not mapped as built.

findings.path: A 3-column table: row 1 = A, B rowspan=2, C; row 2 = D colspan=2, E; row 3 = F, G. In row 2 the walk places D at column 0, advances col by 2 without looking at carry[1] (B's row span), so position (2,1) is covered twice and carry[1] is still 1; in row 3 the carry is consumed at column 1, so position (3,1) is covered by nothing. No error is reported.
findings.impact: A table whose cells overlap and leave a hole loads without a load error and is accepted by set_table (the editor's check is the same function). The grid, the table editor and the PDF then draw it by guessing, and another reader that places cells as SRS-111 says disagrees with Mellon about which cell sits where.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p21_table_tiling.py prints 'loaded without a load error', 'table_geometry_errors: []' and 'set_table accepted it' for that table.
findings.fix: While advancing over a cell's column span, check carry[k] == 0 for every k in col..col+cs-1 and report 'row r: cell at column c overlaps a row span from above' otherwise. Add the table above as a test for loader, editor and validator.

findings.path: (1) A manifest whose enum attribute has no option, whose <parent> lacks doc, whose attribute lacks name or kind or has an unknown kind, or whose <ref> lacks id: the LoaderError message doesn't start with the file's path, so _error_file returns None and DocLoadError.file is None. (2) Any load error that isn't an XML syntax error (duplicate attr, id/stem mismatch, wrong root, bad span, bad table geometry, bad filter op): _doc_load_error takes the line only from XMLSyntaxError.lineno, so line is None although the reason concerns one element on one line.
findings.impact: The Project Explorer tooltip and message box show only the document folder, MCP list_documents returns load_error.file = null, and mellon-check prints no file for the manifest cases; for the others nobody is told the line. The user has to search the files for the broken element.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p1_load_error_fields.py prints 'A: file=None line=None' (enum without option), 'B: file=None line=None' (<parent/>), 'C: file=C/objects/C-0.xml line=None' (duplicate attr on line 4), 'D: ... line=None' (id mismatch on line 2); only the syntax error E gets line=3.
findings.fix: Raise every LoaderError with the file path and the offending element's sourceline (pass path into _parse_parents/_parse_attributes/_parse_refs; add a `line` attribute to LoaderError and read it in _doc_load_error instead of err.__cause__.lineno).

findings.where: MELLON-STORE-SRS-46, MELLON-STORE-SRS-84, MELLON-STORE-SRS-87, MELLON-STORE-SRS-105; mellon/src/mellon/loader.py:310-313 (_text); mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:612-615 (set_description), 584-585 (set_attribute)
findings.path: An object file (hand-written, from another tool or a newer Mellon) holds The pump shall always stop within 2 s. or because of safety. _text returns elem.text only, the text before the first child node. set_description then sets description.text and keeps the child and its tail.
findings.impact: The description reads 'The pump shall' and the rationale 'because': the rest of the requirement silently disappears from the grid, Compare, search and the PDF, although SRS-46 says an undefined element is read as if absent (giving 'The pump shall stop within 2 s.'). After the user retypes the description, the file still holds 'always stop within 2 s.' behind the new text, which the next reader that does read it shows again.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p2_description_child.py prints read description 'The pump shall', read rationale 'because', and after set_description the file holds 'New textalways stop within 2 s.' while it reads back as 'New text'. Same _text is used for table cells and metadata fields.
findings.fix: Read text elements as elem.text plus the tails of their child nodes (skipping undefined elements and comments as SRS-46 says), and have each writer of a text element remove its child nodes before setting text (or refuse an element with children).

findings.path: set_attribute(obj, 'rationale', '') sets existing.text = '' and lxml writes <attr name="rationale"></attr>. Any later operation that rewrites the file, e.g. set_attribute(obj, 'type', 'Note') when type already is Note, re-parses it (text None) and writes <attr name="rationale"/>.
findings.impact: A file Mellon wrote changes bytes under an operation that leaves its canonical form unchanged, so git shows a change nobody made, the object's last commit moves when it is committed, and every link to the object turns suspect. MCP update_object and the GUI's save of an unchanged field reach this path.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p3_empty_element_bytes.py prints 'canonical form equal: True' and 'bytes equal: False' (<attr name="rationale"></attr> became <attr name="rationale"/>).
findings.fix: Write an empty value as text None everywhere (set_attribute, set_description, create_object, remove_attr_option, cells), so Mellon has one written form for an empty element (<x/>, as Proposed SRS-206 states), or skip the write when the serialised bytes equal the file's bytes.

findings.path: A links file indented by 4 spaces or tabs (hand-written, or from another tool). ack_all -> write_ack parses it, sets ack and calls _write_tree without etree.indent.
findings.impact: The file Mellon writes keeps the foreign indentation, so it isn't in the written form; the next edit of that links file (add_link, remove_link) re-indents it, producing a layout-only diff in a later commit. Every other writer calls etree.indent first.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p4_ack_indent.py: after ack_all the file still reads '    <link target-doc="DOC" target-id="DOC-1" type="verifies" ack="5eecbec"/>' with 4 spaces.
findings.fix: Call etree.indent(tree, space="  ") in write_ack, or move the indent into _write_tree so no writer can skip it.

findings.path: Attach or replace a figure (GUI Figure menu, MCP set_figure, a new draw.io figure) or copy an object with its figure: shutil.copyfile opens figures/<id>.svg with 'wb' (truncating it) and copies into it directly, not through a temporary file and os.replace. Mellon is killed or the machine stops after the first chunk.
findings.impact: The figure file holds neither the old nor the new SVG; the figure shows as broken, the draw.io diagram in it is lost, and the half file is what the next commit takes. copy_object's copy also skips _touch, so it isn't in any journal: an error later in the same call leaves the copied figure behind.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p5_figure_crash.py replaces a 51-byte figure with a 200,047-byte one and stops the process after the first write: 'figure after the stop: 4096 bytes; NEITHER (truncated)'.
findings.fix: Copy through git_ops._replace_file(dest, src_path.read_bytes()) (temporary sibling + os.replace) in set_figure and copy_object, and _touch the destination in copy_object.

findings.path: A filter file with <rule kind="attr" attr="type" value="Heading"/> (no op) or op="": `op = el.get("op") or ""` and `if op and op not in _ALL_ATTR_OPS` let the empty code through. create_filter/set_filter_rules with FilterRule(op="") pass _validate_rules (`if rule.op and ...`) and write op="".
findings.impact: A damaged filter file loads without the load error SRS-148 requires; the filter then fails or matches nothing when applied. Mellon itself writes such a file when an agent sends a rule without an operator.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p6_filter_op.py: the file without op loads ('loaded, filters: [('no-op', [('attr', 'type', '', 'Heading')])]'); create_filter writes '<rule kind="attr" op="" attr="type" value="x"/>' and the document still loads; op="equals" is a load error as expected.
findings.fix: In _parse_filter require op in _ALL_ATTR_OPS for kind attr (drop the `op and` guard); in _validate_rules refuse an empty op the same way.

findings.path: is_drawio_svg checks only the root's local name (any namespace) and then searches the decoded content for the substrings '<mxfile' or '<mxGraphModel'.
findings.impact: Figures that SRS-132 says aren't draw.io figures are treated as draw.io figures: content with an mxGraphModel root and no mxfile, content whose root is another element holding an mxfile, content that isn't XML at all ('<mxfileX'), and an svg root outside the SVG namespace. Edit in draw.io and the export's draw.io rendering are then offered for them; a second implementation following SRS-132 classifies the same file differently.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p7_drawio_test.py prints True for 'mxGraphModel root, no mxfile', 'other root holding mxfile', 'not XML: <mxfileX' and 'root svg in another namespace'.
findings.fix: Parse the decoded content with a safe parser and test root.tag == 'mxfile', and require root.tag == '{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}svg'; or, if bare mxGraphModel content must stay editable, say so in SRS-132.

findings.path: set_metadata(doc, 'date', '20261113') and the composite write tools (new_object, update_object, bulk_set_attribute, add_attribute's default) check a date with date.fromisoformat alone, which on Python 3.11+ also takes 20261113 and the week date 2026-W46-5. validator.is_date, which matches YYYY-MM-DD first, isn't used there.
findings.impact: Mellon writes a manifest date or an attribute value that isn't YYYY-MM-DD; validation then reports META_BAD_DATE / ATTR_BAD_DATE on Mellon's own write, and the PDF cover prints the odd form. The composite tools do check dates, but with a different rule from validation's, so an agent can't trust either. (The single set_attribute tool checks no kind at all: that is Proposed MELLON-EDIT-SRS-11, not reported here.)
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p8_metadata_date.py (Python 3.12.13): "'20261113': written, manifest date='20261113', validation=['META_BAD_DATE']", the same for '2026-W46-5'; update_object with due='20261113' prints "written as '20261113', validation=[..., 'ATTR_BAD_DATE']".
findings.fix: Use validator.is_date in set_metadata and _validate_value_for_attr (and in filter._compare_date for filter values, SRS-151).

findings.path: MCP add_link with link_type "" (or add_parent with parent_doc ""): the editor writes type="" / <parent doc=""/>, which the loader rejects. The service's _reload then raises ServiceError(LOAD); _recorded's journal has rollback=False and the listeners aren't called. With the GUI's cache, _reload has already dropped the document while _loaded_all stays True, so get_all_documents returns the list without the document and load_errors() doesn't name it.
findings.impact: The agent gets ok:false with a LoaderError and believes nothing changed, but the file was written and the whole document now fails to load (every edit of it refused, deletes anywhere in the repository refused). A GUI edit whose re-read fails the same way says 'Edit failed' while the write landed, records no undo step, and the document vanishes from the cached document list without a load error until a full refresh.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p9_empty_type.py: 'add_link raised: ErrorCode.LOAD', the links file holds '<link target-doc="DOC" target-id="DOC-1" type="" .../>', the cached service lists 'documents [] load errors []', a fresh load lists 'load errors [('DOC', ...<link> requires @target-doc, @target-id, @type)]'; add_parent('') leaves P with '<parent> missing required @doc'.
findings.fix: Refuse an empty link type and an empty or non-document-ID parent before writing; in the service, on a failed re-read after a write, either roll the write back (journal with rollback) or report it as written-but-unloadable; make RepoCache.invalidate clear _loaded_all (or record the load error) so the list never loses a document.

findings.where: MELLON-STORE-SRS-81, MELLON-STORE-SRS-129 (and SRS-18's rationale that Windows and Linux see the same documents); mellon/src/mellon/loader.py:270-272 (_has_suffix), 94 (load_document)
findings.path: objects/DOC-7.XML or figures/DOC-0.SVG in a commit. _has_suffix compares os.path.normcase(name), which lower-cases on Windows and is the identity on Linux.
findings.impact: On Windows the file is read as object DOC-7 (and DOC-0 gets a figure); on Linux CI the same commit has no object DOC-7 and no figure, so mellon-check, coverage and links differ between a workstation and CI. An editor write then goes to DOC-7.xml, which on Windows is the same file under another name.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p11_suffix_case.py on Windows: 'objects read: ['DOC-0', 'DOC-7']  figure of DOC-0: figures/DOC-0.svg' and 'posix rule would match DOC-7.XML: False'. The Linux side is analysis (posixpath.normcase is the identity).
findings.fix: Compare the suffix case-sensitively (name.endswith('.xml'), '.svg') on every system, as has_manifest already does for the manifest; Proposed SRS-50/SRS-53 then report the odd name.

findings.path: Stored text that bypasses _sanitize_text: a view's column names, a filter condition's attribute name, a parent document ID. lxml refuses the control character with ValueError, which the service maps to VALIDATION.
findings.impact: The operation is refused, but the error says 'All strings must be XML compatible: Unicode or ASCII, no NULL bytes or control characters' without naming the character, so the user or agent can't find it.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p15_sanitize_coverage.py: 'view column name \x01', 'filter rule attr \x01' and 'parent doc id \x01' get the lxml message; description, link type, view name, title and label get 'contains control character U+0001'.
findings.fix: Run _sanitize_text over every string written into a data file (column names, filter attr, parent IDs, outline IDs), or catch lxml's ValueError and name the offending character.

findings.path: History tab -> view an object at a commit: RepoController.object_at_commit parses the blob with its own reader instead of loader.parse_object_bytes / parse_links_bytes.
findings.impact: The object-at-commit view shows an object without its table, takes the last of two attr elements with one name instead of reporting the load error, ignores an id that differs from the file name, silently drops incomplete link elements, and a blob that isn't well-formed raises an uncaught XMLSyntaxError (error dialog) instead of a load error.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p18_historical_reader.py: for a blob with two type attrs, a table and id DOC-9 in DOC-1.xml the historical reader returns 'DOC-9 {'type': 'Heading'} table: None', where the loader reports "filename stem 'DOC-1' does not match @id='DOC-9'"; a blob that isn't well-formed raises lxml.etree.XMLSyntaxError.
findings.fix: Use loader.parse_object_bytes and parse_links_bytes (which apply the same rules) and map LoaderError to ServiceError(LOAD).

findings.path: A folder at the repository root whose contents the user may not examine (a build or cache folder created by another account or a container, an ACL on a share; on Linux any folder without search permission). has_manifest calls Path.is_file(), which re-raises PermissionError (only ENOENT-like errors are swallowed); discover_documents doesn't catch it, nor do load_all, DocumentService.get_all_documents or check.main.
findings.impact: The whole repository fails to open: the GUI gets an uncaught exception instead of a list, every MCP tool that lists documents fails, and mellon-check ends with a traceback (exit 1, read by CI as 'problems found' rather than 2 'unusable root'). One unreadable folder that may not even be a document hides every document, against SRS-28.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p10_unreadable_folder.py (Windows, icacls deny on build/ and build/build.xml): 'load_all raised PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied: ...\\build\\build.xml' and 'service raised PermissionError'.
findings.fix: In has_manifest/discover_documents treat an OSError other than not-found as 'this folder can't be examined': list the folder with a load error when its listing or manifest can't be read (SRS-27), and never let it abort the other documents.

findings.path: New sibling makes two service writes, create_object then move_object(after=sel), with no journal around both. The second fails (the manifest held by another program past the 0.25 s retry, a full disk).
findings.impact: The action reports 'New sibling failed' but the object it created stays, as the last child of the parent instead of after the selected object; the window records it as its own undo step, so the user sees a failure and a new object at once.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p17_new_sibling.py makes the same two calls with the manifest made read-only before the move: 'New sibling failed: IO [WinError 5] ...', then 'objects now: ['DOC-0', 'DOC-1', 'DOC-2', 'DOC-3']' and the outline under the heading 'DOC-1', 'DOC-2', 'DOC-3' (the new DOC-3 last, not after DOC-1).
findings.fix: Give the service a create_object(after=...) that writes the outline once, or wrap both calls in one editor.journal() so a failure of the move rolls back the create, and record them as one undo step.

findings.path: The user opens a bare repository folder (reqs.git), which has no work tree. discover_repo takes the parent of the git folder as the root because repo.workdir is None, so check_repo_root reports a subfolder of a work tree.
findings.impact: The refusal says 'is not the root of its git work tree (<parent>)' and the GUI adds 'Open <parent> instead.'; opening the parent then says 'not inside a git repository'. The reason given is the wrong one of SRS-12's four, and the root named isn't a work tree's root.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p14_bare_repo.py prints '...\\reqs.git is not the root of its git work tree (...\\mellon-store-bare-...)' and for that parent '... is not inside a git repository'.
findings.fix: In check_repo_root return the 'not inside a git work tree' reason when repo.is_bare (or repo.workdir is None), and don't offer a root in _repo_root_advice for that case.

findings.path:
set_description writes '
  indented first line
last
' as given; the loader strips it to 'indented first line
last'.
findings.impact: SRS-89 says each line break of a description is kept; SRS-217 says reading removes whitespace at the start and end. The code follows SRS-217, so a leading or trailing line break (and the leading indentation of the first line) is lost on read while it stays in the file; the next save of that text then rewrites the file. Proposed SRS-216/218 would settle it.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/store/p12_damaged_files.py: "written: '\\n  indented first line\\nlast\\n'" and "read   : 'indented first line\\nlast'".
findings.fix: Say in SRS-89 that it covers line breaks between non-whitespace text, or build SRS-216 (strip on write) so read and written text agree.

findings.path: required="TRUE", header="True" and keep-ancestors="FALSE" are read through .lower(); keep-ancestors="" is read as true; required="yes" and header="1" are read as false without a message.
findings.impact: The requirements say the attribute 'holds true' (or false); a second implementation that compares exactly reads a hand-edited required="TRUE" as optional, so two readers disagree on whether an attribute is required, and a typo such as required="ture" silently makes it optional.
findings.proof: analysis: `a.get("required", "false").lower() == "true"`, `r.get("header", "false").lower() == "true"`, `(root.get("keep-ancestors") or "true").lower()`.
findings.fix: Decide whether other letter cases are accepted; if not, compare exactly and report another value (as a load or validation error, per Proposed SRS-45).

findings.path: A rule kind="attr" with op="present" (or "absent"), or a rule kind="has-outgoing" with op="eq": each code is in SRS-148's list, but the loader checks attr rules against the attribute operators and link rules against present/absent only, and raises a load error.
findings.impact: SRS-148 gives a load error only for codes outside its list, and SRS-149 says an operator that doesn't fit what is tested still loads; the code makes the whole document a load error for these files. A reader built from the requirements loads them.
findings.proof: analysis: _ALL_ATTR_OPS is the union of OPS_BY_KIND, which holds no present/absent; `if op not in LINK_OPS` refuses eq for link rules.
findings.fix: State in SRS-148 which codes each rule kind takes (attr: the attribute operators; has-outgoing/has-incoming: present, absent), or load such rules and report them when the filter is applied.

findings.path: _with_conflict_note looks only for a line starting with seven '<'. The defined term Conflict markers needs that line, a later ======= line and a later >>>>>>> line.
findings.impact: A load error is labelled '(unresolved merge conflict?)' for a file holding only an opening marker line (a half-cleaned conflict or text pasted into a comment), which sends the user to Resolve merge when there is no merge; a reader following the definition doesn't add the note.
findings.proof: analysis: `_CONFLICT_MARKER = re.compile(rb"^<{7}", re.MULTILINE)` is the only test.
findings.fix: Match the three markers in order (^<{7}, then ^={7}, then ^>{7}) as definitions.md defines them.

findings.path: A parse is kept when time.time_ns() (the local clock) minus the file's st_mtime_ns (the file system's clock and resolution) is at least 2 s. On FAT/exFAT the modified time has 2 s resolution and is rounded down, and on a share the server's clock can run behind the local one.
findings.impact: A file read shortly after a write can already count as older than 2 s and be kept; a second write of the same size in the same time slot then isn't read again, so F5, validation and the edits' own checks in a running GUI or MCP server show and use the old content (mellon-check starts with an empty cache and isn't affected). Is this window acceptable until SRS-181 is built?
findings.proof: analysis, unconfirmed: needs a FAT volume or a share with a skewed clock.
findings.fix: Compare against the file system's own time (e.g. the folder's mtime after a probe write) or keep no parse whose mtime is within 2 s of any later stat; SRS-181's content test removes the question.

findings.where: MELLON-TRACE-SRS-4, -43, -130 (definitions.md: last change); mellon/src/mellon/link_index.py:184 (_walk); mellon/src/mellon/git_ops.py:106,112 (last_commit_for_paths); mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:1977 (_compute_ack)
findings.path: Target A-0 committed (C1), deleted by commit C2, its files put back in the working copy without a commit. Or target A-1 whose figure is committed and whose object file never was. Then add_link B-0 -> A-0 (GUI, MCP), or acknowledge a never-reviewed link to it (ack_suspects, Inspector Ack). _walk counts the deletion, or the figure alone, as the object's last change and returns that commit; _compute_ack only checks that the object file is on disk.
findings.impact: definitions.md says an object whose file isn't at the latest commit has no last change, so SRS-4 wants no acknowledged commit and SRS-43 forbids OK. Instead the link records the deleting commit (or the figure's commit) and reads OK in the gutter, Inspector, suspects and export warning, against text that no commit holds and nobody reviewed.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p2_no_last_change.py prints 'case 1: add_link recorded ack = 4a56cd7 | C1 = 42a847d | C2 (the deletion) = 4a56cd7', 'case 1: link state = ok', 'case 1b: acknowledged 1 link(s); state now = ok', and 'case 2: add_link recorded ack = 2eefcc1 (C3 = 2eefcc1) | state = ok'.
findings.fix: In current_hashes and last_commit_for_paths return None for an object whose object file isn't in HEAD's tree (check the HEAD listing before walking). add_link and ack_all then record nothing and the link reads suspect, which is also what SRS-48 and SRS-133 (Proposed) ask.

findings.path: A links file from another clone or a hand edit records ack="HEAD" (or a branch, a tag, HEAD~1). review_suspect_link hands it to repo.revparse_single, which resolves any revision expression. Second case: the recorded 7 digits begin a blob's hash; show_blob_at peels the blob to a commit outside its try block.
findings.impact: With ack="HEAD" the tool returns ack_found true and changed_fields [] for a suspect link whose target changed after the link was made; the tool's description says an empty list means only formatting changed, so an agent acknowledges a change nobody reviewed. With a blob prefix the call fails with InvalidSpecError instead of answering ack_found false and changed fields unknown.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p13_ack_names_blob.py prints "P13b ack='HEAD': state = suspect | ack_found = True | changed_fields = [] | parent_text_at_ack = 'parent v2: changed after the link, never reviewed'" and 'P13 review_suspect_link raises: InvalidSpecError ... can not be successfully peeled into a commit'.
findings.fix: Look an ack up only as a hexadecimal prefix of a commit hash (7 digits or more, object type commit, unambiguous; SRS-51 and SRS-52 are Proposed); anything else gives ack_found false and changed_fields None. Move the peel in show_blob_at inside its try.

findings.path: scan_suspects raises ServiceError(GIT) because discover_repo fails from the document folder (the .git folder moved or the ownership check refuses it after the window opened). object_view gives each outgoing link state=LinkState.OK with reason 'not in a git repo'; the Inspector paints [OK] in the OK colour and shows the reason only for non-OK rows; build_link_states keeps its existence-based 'ok'; suspect_statuses returns [], so the banner hides.
findings.impact: A broken or suspect link shows as OK in the Inspector and the gutter, with no banner: the wrong OK SRS-43 forbids and a review can't catch. MCP inspect_object labels the same case 'unknown'.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p6_gui_qt.py (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen) prints 'P6 Inspector row: A-0 state = OK' for a link whose target file was deleted, "P6 gutter (outgoing, incoming) for B-0 = ('ok', 'none')" and 'P6 suspect_count(B) for the banner = 0'. That a live session reaches it is analysis: open_repo checks the root, so the repository has to become undiscoverable later.
findings.fix: Never report OK for a state that wasn't worked out: add an unknown state (SRS-70, Proposed) or at least show these rows as not checked, drop the 'ok' fallback in build_link_states, and have the banner say the link states couldn't be read.

findings.path: GUI (cached service): delete A-0, which B-0 links to, with force, then Ctrl+Z. _replay invalidates A and B; the window reloads A only (controller.reload_document); RepoCache.get_all keeps returning its snapshot, now without B, because _loaded_all stays True.
findings.impact: After the undo the Inspector shows no incoming links for A-0, the gutter loses the incoming mark, trace down is empty and coverage of A by B fails with 'target document B not in repo', although B's link is back on disk. It lasts until something reloads B (its own window, F5); Redo does the same.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p5_cache_after_undo.py prints "after undo: documents in snapshot = ['A']", 'after undo: incoming(A-0) = []', 'after undo: trace_down(A-0) = []' and "coverage_report(A, B) raises: target document 'B' not in repo".
findings.fix: In _replay reload each affected document that loads (self._load) instead of only invalidating it, or make RepoCache.invalidate clear _loaded_all so the next get_all_documents does a full load.

findings.path: MCP add_link(source_doc='B', source_id='B-0', target_doc='A', target_id='A-0', link_type=''). editor.add_link sanitises the type but doesn't refuse it empty and writes type=""; the service's reload then fails, because the loader requires @type; the tool answers ok false with affected_files [].
findings.impact: The links file is written and the whole source document stops loading (each tool on it fails; suspects() for the repository is refused), while the agent is told nothing was written. new_object and update_object refuse the same input, and the GUI picker strips and refuses it.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p4_empty_link_type.py prints the written '<link target-doc="A" target-id="A-0" type="" ack="4f52889"/>' and 'document B now FAILS TO LOAD: ... <link> requires @target-doc, @target-id, @type'.
findings.fix: Refuse in editor.add_link, before any write, a link type with no character other than whitespace (SRS-13, Proposed); at the least refuse the empty string.

findings.where: MELLON-TRACE-SRS-24 (and copy_object, which reaches MELLON-TRACE-SRS-5 and -6); mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py:883 (DocumentService._validate_composite_links) against mellon/src/mellon/editor.py:1351, 1361 (add_link); writes at document.py:944, 1052, 1166
findings.path: (1) Document X loads with a hand-written object X-1a (file stem equals @id, but not an object ID). update_object(X, X-0, description=..., add_links=[X/X-1a]) or new_object(X, links=[X/X-1a]): the pre-check finds X-1a among the loaded objects; editor.add_link's target_exists needs an object ID and refuses after the description, the removals or the new object were written. (2) copy_object of an object linking into a document that is no longer a parent: the pre-check tests only existence, editor.add_link refuses the parent rule after the copy was created. _recorded opens the journal with rollback=False, so nothing is put back.
findings.impact: A refused call changes files (SRS-24): X-0's description is rewritten, or X-1 is created without its link. copy_object leaves a half-made copy without its links while reporting 'stopped after 0 successful copies' and partial.new_ids [], against its own comment 'so no copy is left half made'; an agent that retries makes another one.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p3_refused_link_writes.py prints "update_object files changed on disk: ['objects\\X-0.xml']", 'description now: CHANGED BY A REFUSED CALL' and "new_object files changed on disk: ['X.xml', 'objects\\X-1.xml']"; codeview-probe/trace/p11_review_and_copy.py prints "P12 copy_object ok = False | error = copy_object stopped after 0 successful copies: 'B' is not allowed to link to 'A'..." and "objects before: ['B-0'] after: ['B-0', 'B-1'] | links of new objects: {}".
findings.fix: Pre-check each link with exactly add_link's tests (suspects.target_exists and the parent rule), and run each composite write (create_object_full, update_object, copy_object) inside one rollback journal so a late refusal puts every file back. SRS-10 (Proposed) decides what a copy does with a refused link.

findings.path: A document folder in the work tree is a symbolic link (checked out on Linux or macOS, or Windows with core.symlinks) or a junction to a folder outside the repository. discover_documents accepts it (is_dir and has_manifest follow links); load_all reads its files; incoming_links, trace, coverage and suspects() use them. An object file that is a link is followed the same way by target_exists.
findings.impact: Working out incoming links, traces and link states opens files outside the repository, which SRS-79 prohibits: another project's links show as incoming links and as the trace, and a link to a network share would make Windows offer the user's credentials.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p8_linked_folder.py (a junction) prints 'EVIL resolves to: ...\\cvtrace-other-project-...\\EVIL | inside repository: False', "incoming_links(A, A-0): [{'source_doc': 'EVIL', 'source_id': 'EVIL-0', 'link_type': 'verifies'}]", and suspects() and trace list EVIL-0.
findings.fix: Treat a document folder, or an entry in it, that is a link or junction as a load error without opening it (MELLON-STORE-SRS-229, Proposed), and check that a resolved path stays under the repository root before opening it.
findings.status: fixed on branch fix/security, 2026-11-14: kept out of this file until fixed because it is a security finding; see docs/open-questions.md Q20

findings.where: MELLON-TRACE-SRS-16, -17 (link picker); mellon/src/mellon/gui/dialogs/link_picker.py:115 (LinkPicker._populate); parent IDs unchecked in mellon/src/mellon/loader.py:329 (_parse_parents)
findings.path: A manifest from another clone declares <parent doc="//fileserver/share"/> or an absolute path. Ctrl+L on an object of that document: _populate lists root / doc_id / 'objects' for each declared parent, and pathlib turns an absolute or UNC parent ID into that path.
findings.impact: Opening the link picker lists a folder outside the repository; with a UNC parent, Windows contacts the host and offers the user's credentials. SRS-79 closes this vector for link states, but its list leaves out the picker.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p6_gui_qt.py (part P7) prints 'P7 link picker listed: C:\\...\\cvtrace-outside-...\\objects | inside repository: False' and 'P7 a UNC parent ID joins to: \\\\fileserver\\share\\ (a network path)'.
findings.fix: List only parents that are document IDs (schema.is_document_id) and loaded documents, using svc.get_loaded_document(doc_id).folder; MELLON-STORE-SRS-230 (Proposed) states the rule, and SRS-79's list could name the link picker.

findings.path: trace(doc, obj, max_depth=0): _trim_tree(edges, -1) returns the depth-1 edges with their children cut, the same answer as max_depth=1.
findings.impact: A max_depth of 0 returns the object's direct neighbours instead of the object alone, as SRS-170's rationale says it should; inspect_object's trace_depth=0 does the same (its description says so, handed to MELLON-MCP-SRS).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p1_trace_depth0.py prints "trace max_depth=0: up = [('A', 'A-0')]", the same as for max_depth=1, and the same for inspect_object trace_depth=0.
findings.fix: In trace return no edges when max_depth is 0 (up_edges = [] if max_depth == 0 else _trim_tree(...)); align inspect_object once MELLON-MCP-SRS settles its depth count.

findings.path: Ctrl+L, type any text into the link type box (it is editable), pick a target, OK.
findings.impact: The list offers exactly satisfies, verifies, refines and implements, but the box takes any typed type, so the GUI makes the link types that SRS-17's rationale leaves to MCP. A typo (Verifies, verfies) makes a link that coverage by link type silently doesn't count.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p6_gui_qt.py prints "P7 link type box editable: True | items: ['satisfies', 'verifies', 'refines', 'implements']"; selected() returns currentText().strip().
findings.fix: setEditable(False); or, if typing is wanted, change SRS-17 to say the list offers these four.

findings.path: ack_suspects(doc) without link_keys while a link of the document is suspect and its target was never committed (current_hash None). ackable leaves the link out; skipped is filled only when link_keys is given.
findings.impact: The call answers ok true, 'acknowledged 0 suspect link(s)', skipped [] while the link stays suspect, so an agent reads it as nothing left to review. With link_keys the same link is reported as skipped with its reason.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p9_ack_suspects.py prints "P9 ack_suspects(B) -> {'ok': True, 'message': 'acknowledged 0 suspect link(s)', 'acknowledged': [], 'skipped': []}" and then "P9 suspects(B) after: [('A-1', 'suspect')]".
findings.fix: Report each suspect link left out in skipped, with its reason, in the no-link_keys case too (SRS-156, Proposed, removes the case later).

findings.path: A new process; ack_suspects(doc, dry_run=True) where a target's last change lies 50 or more commits back. The scan behind the dry run walks the history and _save writes .git/mellon-link-index.json.
findings.impact: Read strictly, 'change no file' is broken: the dry run (and the suspects tool, on a read-only server too) writes a file inside .git. It is a cache outside the work tree and may be meant to fall outside 'file'; the requirement doesn't say.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p9_ack_suspects.py prints 'P10 index file before dry run: False' and 'P10 index file after dry run: True 133'.
findings.fix: Say in SRS-142 (and in the read-only server's requirement) whether Mellon's cache under .git counts, or skip _save during a dry run and on a read-only server.

findings.path: A commit rewraps the target's description (<description>\n    Text\n  </description>) without changing the text Mellon reads (the loader strips it). review_suspect_link parses both blobs with its own parser, which doesn't strip, and compares raw text.
findings.impact: changed_fields says ['description'] and parent_text_now differs from show_object's description only in whitespace, so the reviewer looks for a change Mellon's own model doesn't have. Attribute values are read unstripped the same way.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/trace/p11_review_and_copy.py prints "P11 state: suspect | changed_fields: ['description']", "parent_text_at_ack: 'The pump shall stop.' | parent_text_now: '\\n    The pump shall stop.\\n  '" and "show_object description: 'The pump shall stop.'".
findings.fix: Parse both versions with the loader's object parser (as parse_links_bytes does for links) and compare the RequirementObject fields.

findings.path: svc.trace_up or trace_down raises ServiceError: the document is missing from the cached snapshot (the undo case above) or no longer loads. _populate catches it and shows '(no outgoing links)' or '(no incoming links)'.
findings.impact: A failure reads as an object with no links, so a reviewer concludes nothing derives from or verifies the requirement.
findings.proof: analysis: both except ServiceError branches set the edges to () and fall through to the same placeholder an empty trace gets.
findings.fix: Show the error in the root item or a message instead of the 'no links' placeholder.

findings.path: Objects A->B, A->C, B->D, C->D, D->E. trace_up(A): seen is per path (next_seen = seen | {key}), so D and E are expanded under B and again under C.
findings.impact: The docstring says a diamond 'shows children once'; the code repeats them. A reader trusting it misjudges trace sizes: stacked diamonds grow the trace exponentially (the cost SRS-162, Proposed, addresses), and the trace view expands the whole tree.
findings.proof: analysis: _walk_up and _walk_down pass next_seen down one path only; nothing records objects already expanded on a sibling path.
findings.fix: Correct the docstring now; build SRS-161 and SRS-162 when accepted.

findings.path: Text typed in the filter box, then Suspects only on.
findings.impact: Suspect objects that don't match the filter box text are hidden too. definitions.md's active filter is the saved filter, not the filter box, so read literally SRS-93 is broken; read as 'every narrowing the grid applies', it is met.
findings.proof: analysis: filterAcceptsRow ANDs the saved filter's match set, the suspect state and the filter box text.
findings.fix: Say in SRS-93 whether the filter box applies too.

findings.path: MCP add_link with link_type 'verifies\u0001', or with a carriage return in it.
findings.impact: The first is refused ('contains control character U+0001') though it holds characters other than whitespace; the second is stored with \r turned into \n. Whether SRS-14's 'any text' yields to what XML can store isn't said.
findings.proof: analysis: _sanitize_text replaces \r and raises on _XML_ILLEGAL_C0_RE before add_link writes.
findings.fix: Word SRS-14 as any stored text that holds a character other than whitespace, pointing at MELLON-STORE-SRS's stored-text rules.

findings.path: Double-click an incoming link in the Inspector; open the trace view; double-click an object in it.
findings.impact: These Proposed requirements look built: an incoming link's double-click selects its source through the jump handler, the trace view has no depth limit, and a trace view double-click selects the object in its document's Document Editor. Should they move to Implemented once a test case covers them?
findings.proof: analysis: _incoming.itemActivated is connected to _on_link_activated with payload (src_doc, src_id); _populate calls trace_up and trace_down with no limit; _on_double_clicked calls controller.select_object, which routes another document to the jump handler.
findings.fix: Confirm and update the statuses, or record why they stay Proposed.

findings.path: Anyone who can push makes a commit with an empty message (git commit --allow-empty-message) that changes an object file. log_for_path evaluates (commit_obj.message or "").splitlines()[0] on it, and "".splitlines() is [], so IndexError. RepoController.object_history catches only GitError, and git_history only GitError.
findings.impact: The History tab can't show that object's history: selecting it raises an unexpected error. git_history fails with a tool error. Every other user of log_for_path (review_suspect_link, inspect_object's history) breaks on the same commit, and one pushed commit does it for every object it touched.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp1_issue_and_history.py prints 'B log_for_path raised IndexError list index out of range' and 'B git_history raised IndexError'
findings.fix: Take the first line as (commit_obj.message or "").splitlines()[:1] joined, i.e. '' for an empty message; add a test with an empty-message commit.

findings.path: object_history(doc_id, obj_id, max_entries: int = 20) is called by HistoryTab.refresh without max_entries; an object changed in 25 commits.
findings.impact: The History tab lists the newest 20 commits and nothing says older ones exist, so a reviewer reading the object's history takes it for complete. 217 has no limit (225 is the Proposed fix for a cut list).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp3_gui.py prints 'D commits that changed the object: 25 | History tab rows: 20'
findings.fix: Either list every commit (with paging) or keep the cap and add a 'more commits' row as 225 asks; update 217 if a cap is intended.

findings.path: git_history(doc_id, obj_id, max_entries=0) or -1: log_for_path appends the first match and only then tests len(results) >= max_entries.
findings.impact: The tool returns one commit when asked for at most 0 (or a negative number), so the result breaks 'up to max_entries'.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp1_issue_and_history.py prints 'C git_history max_entries=0 -> 1 entries' and '=-1 -> 1 entries'
findings.fix: Refuse max_entries < 1 with an error naming it (224), or test the limit before appending.

findings.path: The History tab keeps only short_hash (7 digits) per row and passes it to object_at_commit, which resolves it with revparse_single. libgit2 resolves a tag or branch name before a hash prefix, and raises ValueError for an ambiguous prefix. In the probe a tag named like commit c1's short hash points at c2.
findings.impact: View at this commit… shows the object at another commit (labelled with that commit's hash, which a reader may not check). In a large repository an ambiguous 7-digit prefix raises an uncaught ValueError instead of showing anything. Compare with latest… passes the same short hash (the Compare part reports its side).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp1_issue_and_history.py prints 'D short hash 4ab45fe of c1 -> shows description: b' (b is c2's text)
findings.fix: Store commit_oid (the full hash log_for_path already returns) in _HASH_ROLE and pass it to object_at_commit and compare_requested; show the short form only.

findings.path: A document's objects were committed (for example commit_changes with paths naming only the object file) but its manifest wasn't. in_last_commit tests tree[rel] for the folder, which HEAD holds, so _refresh_discard_action enables Discard; discard_paths then deletes every file HEAD doesn't hold, the manifest included.
findings.impact: The Discard action is enabled while the latest commit lacks the manifest, and running it deletes the manifest: the document disappears from the repository, which 203 exists to prevent.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp3_gui.py prints 'C HEAD holds DOC/DOC.xml: False', 'C in_last_commit('DOC') -> True' and 'C discard changed: ('DOC/DOC.rules.xml', 'DOC/DOC.xml') | manifest still on disk: False'
findings.fix: Test the manifest's path (<folder>/<doc_id>.xml) in HEAD, and have DocumentService.discard_document_changes refuse on the same condition so the MCP or a script can't do it either.

findings.path: Document A declares parent P and has no link to P yet; P has an uncommitted change. _dirty_parents takes repo.parent_doc_ids, which returns the documents A's links point to, not A's declared parents.
findings.impact: The commit dialog doesn't warn that the parent document P has uncommitted changes, which 150 asks for. The set used is linked documents, direct only, so it is neither 150's declared parents nor 151's upstream documents.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp2_commits.py prints 'F manifest parents of A: ('P',)' and 'F dirty_parents shown for A: ()'
findings.fix: Decide 150 vs 151 (the review chose upstream documents); then use doc.parents, or the transitive upstream walk _upstream_warnings already does.

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-280, MELLON-VER-SRS-279, MELLON-VER-SRS-261, MELLON-VER-SRS-160, MELLON-VER-SRS-167; mellon/src/mellon/gui/dialogs/commit_dialog.py:294 CommitDialog._has_changes; mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:2076 _commit_current_doc
findings.path: The document's metadata has no author, so the dialog prefills git's user.name. _has_changes compares the author field with current_author (''), so the untouched prefill counts as a change; _commit_current_doc writes it to the manifest for the same reason.
findings.impact: With nothing to commit, entering a tag shows Commit, not Tag, and makes a new commit that writes the author (280: tag the latest commit, make no new commit). Raising the issue with no file change is allowed, the commit holding only the unasked-for author write (261). Every commit from such a document writes the author although the user changed nothing.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp3_gui.py prints 'A empty author, no files, tag v1.0: tag_only = False | button = Commit | enabled = True' and, with the issue raised and no files, 'button = Commit | enabled = True'
findings.fix: Compare the fields with their prefill values in _has_changes and in meta_updates; write the author only when the user edits it, or decide that the prefill counts and say so in 160/167.

findings.path: Both patterns are r"^\d+(\.\d+)*$" without re.ASCII: \d matches any Unicode digit and $ matches before a final newline. A user types the issue '２' (fullwidth 2, easy with an East Asian IME).
findings.impact: The dialog and create_issue_tag accept it and create the tag DOC-issue-２; current_issue reads it as 2, so the real '2' is then refused as not higher. The issue tag doesn't match [0-9] patterns in other tools or CI, and looks like issue 2. validate_issue('1\n') also passes (the ref creation then fails). _ISSUE_FORM_RE and _DATE_RE share the flaw.
findings.proof: probes codeview-probe/ver/lp1_issue_and_history.py ('A created issue tag 'DOC-issue-２' current_issue -> '２'', 'A then '2' refused') and codeview-probe/ver/lp3_gui.py ('B issue '２': error = '' | commit enabled = True')
findings.fix: Use [0-9] and fullmatch (or re.ASCII with \Z) in every issue, issue-form and date pattern.

findings.path: A message with lines but no blank line, such as 'Subject\nmore detail', gets sep '\n', so 'Via: mellon-mcp' joins the first paragraph. git (and libgit2) never reads trailers in the title paragraph.
findings.impact: The commit carries no Via trailer by git's definition (definitions: Trailer), so `git log --format=%(trailers)` and any audit that looks for agent commits by trailer miss it, while the text looks right.
findings.proof:
probe codeview-probe/ver/lp2_commits.py prints for 'Subject
more detail': stored='Subject
more detail
Via: mellon-mcp
' trailers={}, while 'Subject

Body' gives trailers={'Via': 'mellon-mcp'}
findings.fix: Always separate the trailer with a blank line unless the last paragraph is already a trailer block (and isn't the title).

findings.path: git_ops.commit maps only pygit2.GitError to GitError. pygit2 raises ValueError for user.name 'Bad <Name>' (angle brackets) and OSError for an absolute path in paths. service.commit catches only GitError, and _auto_commit_if_requested and commit_changes only ServiceError.
findings.impact: A write tool with commit_message writes the file, then raises a tool error: the agent gets neither ok, affected_files nor commit_error, while the write stays on disk (173 says return the commit's error with the result). In the GUI the commit ends in the unexpected-error dialog instead of 'Commit failed'.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp2_commits.py prints 'C MCP edit_metadata(commit_message=...) with that identity: ValueError: failed to parse signature' and 'D service.commit(paths=[<absolute path>]): OSError: could not find ... to stat'
findings.fix: Catch (pygit2.GitError, ValueError, OSError) in git_ops.commit and raise GitError; in _auto_commit_if_requested turn any exception into commit_error.

findings.path: The nothing-to-commit test is 'if head is not None and tree_oid == head.tree.id'. With an unborn HEAD it is skipped: commit(root, msg, []) or a selection that names only a missing path (a typo) builds an empty tree.
findings.impact: The first commit of a repository can be an empty commit reported as success, and an agent's mistyped path reads as committed.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp2_commits.py prints 'A git_commit(paths=[]) on unborn: OK -> ...' with 'new root commit tree entries: 0', and 'A service.commit(paths=['DOC/typo.xml']) on unborn: OK'
findings.fix: For an unborn HEAD refuse when no selected file exists (empty tree_index); better, count the selected files that differ from HEAD and refuse at zero in both cases.

findings.path: git_ops.commit writes the index with the selected paths before create_commit. When create_commit is refused (tip moved, or the branch ref locked), the manifest stays staged with the dialog's author and date. restore_manifest puts back only the working-copy file.
findings.impact: After the failed commit the working copy shows the old author and date but the index holds the dialog's; the next commit made in a git client records an author and date nobody committed (96, Proposed, would forbid this). Mellon's own next commit takes the working copy, so the two disagree.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp2_commits.py prints the refusal ('... nothing was committed: commit again') and 'B status of DOC/DOC.xml after the refused commit: INDEX_MODIFIED= True'; the GUI part is analysis of restore_manifest, which never touches the index
findings.fix: On a failed create_commit, put the selected paths' index entries back as they were (keep a copy of the entries before index.add), or write the index only after the commit.

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-99, MELLON-VER-SRS-102, MELLON-VER-SRS-126, MELLON-VER-SRS-146; mellon/src/mellon/git_ops.py:274 _selected_files, :658 dirty_paths_under
findings.path: A nested git repository sits in a document folder (say a figure library cloned into DOC/figures/work). git status lists it as 'DOC/figures/work/'; dirty_paths_under passes that on, the commit dialog lists it, and _selected_files expands it to itself, so index.add('DOC/figures/work/') fails.
findings.impact: No commit of that document from the commit dialog can succeed, and commit_changes() without paths fails for every document, until the user finds and moves the folder; the only message is "invalid path: 'DOC/figures/work/'". Discard names the case (209); commit doesn't.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp5_nested.py prints "dialog lists: ('DOC/figures/work/', 'DOC/objects/DOC-0.xml')" and "commit_document: ServiceError invalid path: 'DOC/figures/work/'"
findings.fix: Leave nested repositories out of the selection and warn of them in the dialog and the commit result, or refuse with a message that names the folder as a nested git repository.

findings.path: With text typed in the Inspector, the user picks Discard… and then Cancel. _save_pending_edits() runs before QMessageBox.question, as GUI-SRS-74 asks for every action.
findings.impact: The cancelled discard has written the typed text to the object file, while 196 says a cancelled discard changes no file. The two requirements can't both hold; the code follows GUI-SRS-74.
findings.proof: analysis: in _discard_document_changes, self._save_pending_edits() (line 2238) precedes the confirmation; not run in a GUI.
findings.fix: Decide which wins (213, Proposed, drops pending edits on a completed discard): either exempt Discard from GUI-SRS-74 and keep the text pending until the answer, or reword 196 to 'no file other than the pending edits'.

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-230, MELLON-VER-SRS-380; mellon/src/mellon/gui/dialogs/object_at_commit.py:57 ObjectAtCommitDialog.__init__; mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:225 and project_explorer_window.py:168 _git_cell
findings.path: View at this commit… shows each attribute value in QLabel(value), whose text format is AutoText. A value from another clone such as 'Approved Draft' is taken as rich text. The status bar's git cell is a QLabel too, showing the branch name.
findings.impact: The dialog shows a formatted 'Approved Draft' instead of the stored value, so an older version reads differently from its file (230); markup in a pushed value or branch name can hide or fake text (380, Proposed).
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/lp3_gui.py prints 'E label textFormat: TextFormat.AutoText | Qt.mightBeRichText: True'
findings.fix: setTextFormat(Qt.PlainText) on every label that shows repository text.
findings.status: fixed on branch fix/security, 2026-11-14: kept out of this file until fixed because it is a security finding; see docs/open-questions.md Q20

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-149, MELLON-VER-SRS-283, MELLON-VER-SRS-182, MELLON-VER-SRS-183; mellon/src/mellon/service/document.py:2035 prepare_document_commit, :2088 _upstream_warnings; mellon/src/mellon/gui/main_window.py:2482 _refresh_git_cell
findings.path: A suspect scan that raises ServiceError gives an empty suspect list; _upstream_warnings returns [] when the documents can't be read; the status bar count turns any exception into n = 0.
findings.impact: A failure reads as all clear: no unreviewed links, no upstream open points, 'no uncommitted document changes' in the tooltip, with nothing saying a check didn't run.
findings.proof: analysis: the except branches at the cited lines replace the result with an empty one and log nothing; not provoked by a probe.
findings.fix: Show 'couldn't check links/upstream documents/changes: <reason>' in the dialog and the status bar instead of an empty result.

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-119, MELLON-VER-SRS-148, MELLON-VER-SRS-192, MELLON-VER-SRS-206, MELLON-VER-SRS-207, MELLON-VER-SRS-259, MELLON-VER-SRS-276; mellon/src/mellon/git_ops.py _refuse_during_merge, tag_name_error, discard_paths; service/document.py prepare_document_commit, commit_document

findings.path: A repository has a local branch named origin/main (refs/heads/origin/main) and the remote-tracking branch origin/main (refs/remotes/origin/main) at another commit. document_versions labels both 'Branch origin/main'. The user picks the remote-tracking entry; CompareDialog.ref looks the version up by its text, combo.findText(currentText), which returns the first entry with that label, so refs/heads/origin/main is compared. The same text-based lookup takes the History tab's 7-digit hash to the first offered commit it prefixes (_set_ref).
findings.impact: The dialog compares a version the user didn't pick, and the result is labelled 'Branch origin/main (<hash>)', the same words as the version picked; only the 7-digit hash tells them apart. A reviewer can sign off the wrong difference.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/compare/p6_combo.py prints 'user picked: refs/remotes/origin/main' / 'dialog compares: refs/heads/origin/main', and DOC-1 Modified where the picked version equals HEAD and no change was expected.
findings.fix: Take the ref from combo.currentIndex()'s itemData whenever the shown text is that item's label, and fall back to text only for typed text; label remote-tracking branches apart from local ones (e.g. 'Remote branch origin/main'); have the History tab pass the full hash (log_for_path already returns commit_oid).

findings.path: A figure in the working copy can't be read (locked by another program, no permission) while its content equals the latest commit's. _DiskSide keys it ('unreadable', ...), which never equals a blob id, so the object is read; _Reader.figure returns None on OSError; _delta then sees a figure at From and none at To and reports FigureChange(svg, None). ObjectState has no figure error, so the row isn't marked unreadable.
findings.impact: Compare reports the object Modified with its figure deleted, at To; read the other way round, a figure added. The figure is unchanged. SRS-27 covers only object and links files, and SRS-81 (Proposed) only a figure that can't be drawn, so nothing requires the right answer.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/compare/p2_figure.py b) locks the figure's bytes: 'row: DOC-1 [Modified] errors: (None, None)', 'figure at From: True at To: False', MCP row figure {'from': True, 'to': False}.
findings.fix: Keep the OSError for a figure as for object and links files (a figure error in ObjectState, counted in ObjectState.problem), so the row reads 'unreadable at To'; add the figure file to MELLON-VER-SRS-27's wording.

findings.path: A document changed by more than 200 commits on HEAD's history. document_versions offers log_for_path(..., max_entries=200): the newest 200 commits that changed the document.
findings.impact: Older commits that changed the document aren't offered, though SRS-7 says each one is; a user looking for an early version has to know and type its hash. Nothing in the dialog says the list is cut.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/compare/p3_versions.py prints 'commits that changed DOC: 205 offered: 200' and 'oldest commit offered? False'.
findings.fix: Either state the limit in MELLON-VER-SRS-7 (and show 'older commits: type a hash' in the list), or load the rest on demand, which MELLON-VER-SRS-83 needs anyway.

findings.path: Two commits whose figure for DOC-1 differs only by an XML comment. _figure_key writes Canonical XML with_comments=False, so the keys are equal and _delta reports no figure change.
findings.impact: definitions.md says the canonical form is Canonical XML 1.1 'with comments' and that 'comments do' show, so a comment change isn't 'gone in the canonical form', and SRS-22 doesn't allow treating it as no change; whether a comment is part of the figure field isn't stated. The code's docstring takes the opposite reading on purpose. Object, links and manifest files are compared by what they parse to, which also drops comments, but there SRS-74 (Proposed) is the open point.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/compare/p2_figure.py a) prints 'comment-only figure change: no change reported'.
findings.fix: Decide which is meant: either compare figures with comments (with_comments=True), or amend the definition or SRS-22 to say that comments in a figure don't count.

findings.path: compare_document over MCP on an object whose figure changed at both versions: the row carries figure {'from': true, 'to': true}; an added or deleted object carries figure: true.
findings.impact: SRS-59 says the tool returns 'each changed field at both' versions; for the figure an agent gets only whether one exists, so it can't tell what changed, unlike a person in the dialog (SRS-51). 'Agents must get the same answer as a person' (rationale).
findings.proof: analysis: serialize.py:339-342 writes only 'svg_a is not None' and 'svg_b is not None'; p2_figure.py b) shows the shape {'from': True, 'to': False}.
findings.fix: Return the SVG text at both versions (or a size-capped excerpt plus its canonical hash), or state in SRS-59 that a figure is reported by presence only.

findings.path: A result is shown. The user picks another From; compare() replaces the summary, the only place that names the shown result's From and To, with 'Comparing…', while the list keeps the old rows and the From box already shows the new version.
findings.impact: Until the new result arrives, the old rows are shown without their versions and under the new From and To, so they read as the new comparison's result. With a slow comparison (large document, working copy) that lasts seconds; if the user copies the list meanwhile, the header comes from _labels, which is right, but the screen isn't.
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/compare/p7_running.py prints "while the second runs: summary = 'Comparing…' rows shown = 1 From box = '0b874a4  two'".
findings.fix: Keep the old header and add the running comparison to it ('… — comparing 0b874a4 two → HEAD'), or grey out or hide the old rows while a comparison runs.

findings.path: A comparison runs on the thread pool and emits on _CompareSignals, a child QObject of the dialog. The user closes the dialog, or its Document Editor (which deletes the dialog, SRS-5), at the moment the job finishes. The GUI thread deletes the signals object while the pool thread is inside emit().
findings.impact: The RuntimeError guard catches only an object already deleted before the emit; a deletion that overlaps the emit is a data race in Qt (a QObject destroyed while another thread emits its signal) and can crash the GUI, losing pending text. Unconfirmed: a race, not reproduced.
findings.proof: analysis: the signals object is created with parent=self (line 471) and the dialog has WA_DeleteOnClose (line 455); _emit (line 114) checks liveness and emits as two separate steps on another thread.
findings.fix: Create the signals object without a parent, owned by the job (connected to the dialog's slots, which Qt disconnects when the dialog is destroyed), so the emitting object outlives every emit.

findings.path: The trace comment on the message, summary and empty labels' PlainText format cites MELLON-VER-SRS-10, -41 and -34.
findings.impact: Those requirements ask for an error message, the versions and the 'no object changed' text; showing repository text as plain text is MELLON-VER-SRS-380 (Proposed), so the comment points a reader at requirements that don't hold the rule, and a change to -380 won't find this code.
findings.proof: analysis: compare the comment with the text of MELLON-VER-SRS-10, -34, -41 and -380.
findings.fix: Cite MELLON-VER-SRS-380 (Proposed) in the comment.

findings.path: base outline D-1, D-2, D-3; ours moves D-3 to the front (D-3, D-1, D-2); theirs deletes D-1 (D-2, D-3). _positions keys a place by (parent, previous sibling), so theirs' deletion changes D-2's previous sibling and moved_theirs is True for D-2 while moved_ours is False; place() then puts D-2 first as theirs has it
findings.impact: Ours' move of D-3 is undone without a word: the merged outline is D-2, D-3 instead of D-3, D-2. Any insertion or deletion on theirs makes the following sibling count as moved by theirs, which overrides ours' order around it; the definitions say inserting or deleting a sibling moves nothing
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p1_outline.py prints "merged outline: ['D-2', 'D-3'] (expected ['D-3', 'D-2'])", and the nested case H: B, C instead of H: C, B
findings.fix: Decide 'moved on theirs' as the definition of Moved does (parent changed, or not in the largest set of siblings whose order base and theirs share), not by previous sibling, and apply only those moves to ours' outline

findings.path: Delete against change is decided per file, not per object. (a) theirs deletes D-1 (object, links, figure); ours changed only D-1's figure, or only acknowledged D-1's link: the object file is unchanged on ours, so b == ov and the object is deleted; the figure or links file is merged on its own and kept. (b) ours changed D-1's object file, theirs deleted D-1: keep (the preset) restores the object file only; its links file and figure, unchanged on ours, stay deleted
findings.impact: (a) A requirement that one side changed is deleted without the keep/delete choice; the dialog shows a lone 'Figure' choice (figure case) or nothing (links case), and leaves an orphan figure or an orphan links file (a validation error: 'source has no corresponding object'). (b) A kept requirement silently loses its outgoing links and figure, while the dialog's Traces to still lists the dropped link
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p10_delete_vs_figure.py: case A dialog blocks [('D-1', None, ['Figure'])], objects/D-1.xml exists False, figures/D-1.svg exists True; case B dialog blocks [], links/D-1.xml exists True, object gone. p3_keep.py: after keep, links/D-1.xml and figures/D-1.svg exist False while the plan's links list D-1 -> D-2
findings.fix: Group an object's object file, links file and figure, and decide delete against change per object: if one side deleted the object file and the other changed any of the three, offer keep or delete (keep preset); keep takes all three from the changing side, delete removes all three

findings.path: base parents [P1]; ours adds P2 (and retitles, so the manifest conflicts); theirs removes P1
findings.impact: The merged parents are [P2]; MELLON-VER-SRS-321 (Implemented) says each parent either side declares is kept, [P1, P2]. The code lets a one-sided removal win, which is MELLON-VER-SRS-322 (Proposed). git's clean merge of a manifest (the other branch of _merge_manifest) also lets a removal win. The specification's status doesn't match the code
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p2_parents.py prints "merged parents: ['P2'] (321 expects ['P1', 'P2'])"
findings.fix: Since 322 is the decided rule (Q65 answered 2026-11-11) and the code already does it: confirm 322, set it Implemented and withdraw 321 rather than change the code

findings.path: Both sides retitle D (manifest conflict) and change README.md (a conflict outside document folders, so the banner keeps Resolve merge...). Resolve with title FIRST, then Resolve merge... again and choose SECOND. The manifest is no longer conflicted in the index, so _git_merged returns the entry the first resolve staged, and _merge_manifest takes the properties from it instead of merging base, ours and theirs
findings.impact: The second dialog shows no conflict for the document properties and the title stays FIRST: resolving again doesn't start from the commits for metadata, parents and attribute definitions, so the user can't revise those choices (objects are recomputed, the manifest's properties aren't)
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p8_second_resolve.py prints 'plan 2 hands: []' and 'after resolve 2: title = FIRST'
findings.fix: Use git's clean merge only for a path git merged by itself: for example compare the index entry with git's own clean merge of the three blobs (or with the entry recorded before Mellon first wrote it), or always merge the properties field by field from the three commits

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-346, MELLON-VER-SRS-347, MELLON-VER-SRS-354; mellon/src/mellon/gui/dialogs/merge_dialog.py:177 MergeDialog._text_field, mellon/src/mellon/merge.py:493 _merge_object, merge.py:458 _shown_value

findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p4_from_theirs.py prints "conflicts ['Text'] from_theirs ('status',)"

findings.path: (a) a side commits a document file that doesn't parse (for example with conflict markers) and both sides changed it: plan() raises lxml XMLSyntaxError; _resolve_merge catches only MergeError. (b) another program holds index.lock: resolve() rewrites the work-tree files, then index.write() raises pygit2.GitError; the dialog catches only MergeError and OSError
findings.impact: Resolve merge... ends in the unexpected-error dialog instead of a message: (a) the message names a line in '<string>' but neither the file nor the side, so the user can't find what blocks the merge; (b) the files are already rewritten while the conflicts stay, with no word that resolving again finishes it
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p5_malformed.py prints 'uncaught by _resolve_merge: lxml.etree.XMLSyntaxError - StartTag: invalid element name, line 3, column 2 (<string>, line 3)'; p12_lock_and_date.py prints '(a) NOT caught by the dialog: _pygit2 GitError - the index is locked'
findings.fix: Turn a parse error into MergeError naming the path and the side (ours, theirs, base); check index.lock before writing any file and raise MergeError naming the lock; catch pygit2.GitError in the dialog

findings.path: Both sides change the metadata date; the user types 'next week' as the merged text. _clean only sanitises; set_metadata's date check isn't applied
findings.impact: The manifest gets date 'next week', a META_BAD_DATE validation error that blocks the next commit from the Document Editor; the merge commit itself is made in a git client, which doesn't validate
findings.proof: probe codeview-probe/ver/merge/p12_lock_and_date.py prints '(b) date written: next week'
findings.fix: Check a merged date as set_metadata does (is_date) and raise MergeError naming the field, before writing anything

findings.path: 'The object whose creating commit is the later one': the code compares committer times (commit_time) of the first commit on each side, in reverse topological order, that holds the object file; on equal times it renumbers theirs
findings.impact: A rebase or cherry-pick resets the committer time, so an older object can read as the later one and lose its ID; the requirement doesn't say which time counts or what a tie does (the rationale leaves it to test mapping)
findings.proof: analysis: side = "ours" if t_ours > t_theirs else "theirs" with t from commit.commit_time
findings.fix: State committer time and the tie rule in 331's test mapping, or move on to 332-334 as planned

findings.where: MELLON-VER-SRS-340; mellon/src/mellon/gui/dialogs/merge_dialog.py:85 MergeDialog, merge_dialog.py:131 MergeDialog._hand_block, mellon/src/mellon/merge.py:1016 resolve
findings.path: The Renumbered line and each block title are rich text built from an object ID (a file name from another clone) and a branch name read from MERGE_MSG; git allows < > & in branch names. resolve() writes root / path for paths read from the merge's trees without checking they stay in a document folder
findings.impact: A crafted branch or file name can change how the dialog reads (markup in a QLabel). Path escape needs a crafted path on both sides (it must differ in ours and theirs, or be renumbered), and git refuses such paths on checkout, so it is unconfirmed
findings.proof: analysis: _wrapped(..., rich=True) with r.obj_id and self._names[r.side]; target = root / path with no containment check
findings.fix: Escape names with html.escape (MELLON-VER-SRS-380, Proposed) and check each written path with the editor's path guard (MELLON-VER-SRS-329, Proposed) when those are built
